| **OPEN (CC-1 2026-09-04, ROOT CAUSE FOUND, NOT FIXED -- owner order, do not void the invoice, wait for the ruling):** `PROFORMA-MINTED-WITHOUT-PICKUP-LOAD-13508` -- load 13508 (`draft` status, both stops `pending`, zero `actual_arrival_at` anywhere) carries a live `proforma` invoice (`accounting.invoices` display_id 13508, $2,500.00, created 2026-09-04T07:27:37Z), despite LST-F20322's locked ruling ("proforma mints at first pickup, never at book") and `proforma-mint-on-first-pickup.ts`'s own gate (`mintProformaInvoiceOnFirstPickup` requires `actual_arrival_at OR actual_departure_at` non-null on the FIRST pickup stop, confirmed it would have correctly SKIPPED with reason `pickup_not_completed` on this load). **ROOT CAUSE, traced to the exact call site:** `apps/backend/src/accounting/resync-proforma-from-load-rate.ts`'s `resyncProformaInvoiceFromLoadRate`, called from `apps/backend/src/mdata/loads.routes.ts:1832` on every rate-touching PATCH to a load. When no draft/proforma invoice exists yet for the load, this function calls `buildInvoiceFromLoad(..., asProforma: true)` UNCONDITIONALLY -- ZERO pickup check, not the same gate `mintProformaInvoiceOnFirstPickup` enforces. The load's rate was edited at 2026-09-04T07:27:37Z (matching the invoice's `created_at` to the second) -- that PATCH is what minted it. The function's own header comment states its premise: mint here "the same call booking would have made if the rate had existed at book time" -- but `book-load.service.ts`'s own comment (line ~2033) says the opposite: "proforma is minted at first pickup..., never at book." The resync path's founding premise about what booking does is factually wrong, independent of whether the RULING itself has since changed. **This is a real code defect against the currently-cited locked rule, not (as far as I can find) a rule that drifted** -- but the owner rules, not the code; reporting before touching anything, per instruction. Recommended fix, NOT applied: gate `resyncProformaInvoiceFromLoadRate`'s mint-fallback branch on the SAME pickup-completed check `mintProformaInvoiceOnFirstPickup` uses, so a bare rate edit on an unpicked-up load never mints, and the first-pickup path mints naturally once pickup actually happens. | `apps/backend/src/accounting/resync-proforma-from-load-rate.ts`; `apps/backend/src/mdata/loads.routes.ts:1832`; `apps/backend/src/accounting/proforma-mint-on-first-pickup.ts` (correct, uninvolved) | **owner ruling required before any fix** | gate the resync path's mint-fallback on the same pickup-completed check, OR the owner rules this mint is acceptable and the LOCKED RULING itself needs amending instead | live `mdata.loads`/`mdata.load_stops`/`accounting.invoices` reads, bypass_rls, this session; source trace of every `buildInvoiceFromLoad` caller | **OPEN · root cause found · NOT fixed · invoice NOT voided · owner rules next** |

| **FIXED (CC-2 2026-09-01, found while chasing an unrelated board-hygiene push):** `SELFTEST-EXIT-SKIPS-FINALLY-CORRUPTS-BOOK-LOAD-SERVICE` — `scripts/verify-usmca-driver-bill-per-load-rate.mjs`'s `--selftest` called `process.exit(1)` from INSIDE its own `try{...}finally{restore}` on a failing assertion. `process.exit()` terminates the process immediately and does NOT run pending `finally` blocks (unlike throw/return), so a failing selftest left the REAL, money-critical `apps/backend/src/dispatch/book-load.service.ts` (driver-pay-rate resolution) permanently mutated on disk instead of restored — reproduced live, confirmed with `git status` showing the file dirty after the selftest exited. **Root cause of the failure itself, not just the corruption:** the assertion `/load\.driver_pay_rate_per_mile/.test(bookLoad)` is a bare substring-anywhere-in-file check; the file has 4 occurrences of that literal string (the real functional read at the resolution call site, 2 comments, and an unrelated PATCH-side write `load.driver_pay_rate_per_mile = input...`). The selftest's mutation (a non-global `.replace()`) only breaks the FIRST occurrence (the real read), but the assertion still matched the 3 untouched occurrences and passed — meaning the same coverage gap exists for a REAL regression, not just the planted one: if someone silently broke the actual read while leaving the comments/write intact, this guard would not catch it, on a money-critical field. **FIX (this PR):** (1) exit only AFTER the `finally` restores the backup (`let failed` flag, `process.exit(1)` moved outside the try/finally); (2) tightened the assertion to `/perLoadRateDollars\s*=\s*Number\(load\.driver_pay_rate_per_mile/`, anchored to the actual resolution call site. Verified: normal run still passes on real code; `--selftest` passes and correctly detects the planted mutation; forced-failure test (temporarily patched the condition to always-fail) confirms the file is now restored via `git status` even on the failure path. | `scripts/verify-usmca-driver-bill-per-load-rate.mjs` | **CC-2** | fixed at root (exit ordering + assertion precision), not patched around | live: selftest PASS/fails-correctly-and-restores both re-run after the fix; forced-failure re-run shows `git status --short apps/backend/src/dispatch/book-load.service.ts` empty afterward (was dirty before the fix, same forced-failure scenario) | **FIXED · live-verified both halves (finally-skip + coverage gap)** |

| **CORROBORATED (CC-2 2026-09-01, lead-authorized "corroborate, do not rebuild"):** the SKIP-vs-FAIL root cause suspected in the row above is confirmed, precisely, for the two guards spot-checked there. `scripts/verify-static.mjs`'s `noDbEnv()` does NOT unset `DATABASE_URL` — it points it at a dead-port sentinel (`postgresql://verify_static:none@127.0.0.1:59999/...`) so a real-DB attempt fails fast instead of possibly reaching prod. `verify-no-seat-instruction-overrides-owner-void.mjs` and `verify-no-unmanifested-prod-financial-fixtures.mjs` both check `if (!databaseUrl)` for their SKIP branch — that condition is FALSE when `DATABASE_URL` is set to the sentinel (a truthy string), so neither guard takes its SKIP path; both instead attempt to connect and hit an **uncaught `ECONNREFUSED`, crashing with exit 1** — reproduced live, verbatim: `DATABASE_URL="postgresql://verify_static:none@127.0.0.1:59999/verify_static_none" node scripts/verify-no-unmanifested-prod-financial-fixtures.mjs` → `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:59999` (uncaught, unhandled) → exit 1. Same for the sibling guard. Confirmed neither is registered in `scripts/push-gate-capability-policy.mjs`'s `dbGated` capability set (`grep` for both names = 0 hits) — that's WHY `capabilityPreflight()` never intercepts them before running: the policy doesn't know they need a database, so `classify()` proceeds to actually execute them against the dead sentinel instead of pre-emptively marking SKIP-capability. **This is a real, precise, guard-infrastructure bug** (missing policy registration + a guard-side SKIP check that only handles "unset" not "unreachable"), not a stale baseline. **Scope check, not re-audit:** spot-checked 3 more names from the original 37 list (`verify-safety-creator-pickers`, `verify-prod-verified-live-binding`, `verify-program-scoreboard-13gate-prodread`) under the same dead-sentinel env — all 3 now run clean/PASS, meaning the original 37-count has already drifted significantly in the hours since (matches the row above's own caveat) and a fresh full re-run would very likely show a smaller, different set — did not re-run the full 37 (that is the "rebuild"/re-audit scope explicitly not authorized this pass, only corroboration was). (2) The "silence" is **by design, not a bug**: `book-load.service.ts:580-596` checks for a prior skip-audit row (`load_id` + `operating_company_id` match) and returns early **without** writing a new one if found ("one durable skip record per load," comment `:578-579`) — so L-0002's two delivery-transition re-entries (15:08:49, 15:10:23 UTC) both correctly hit this dedupe and produced zero *new* audit rows. Absence of an audit event at a delivery timestamp is the **expected steady state**, never evidence the mint code didn't run — my original finding conflated the two. **DEFECT B, named:** `pingSettlementOnLoadEvent` (`settlements-load-bookended.service.ts:821-891`) opens on `in_transit` (`:855`), closes on `delivered_pending_docs` (`:886-891`) — **no branch for `completed_docs_received`**, falls off the end at `:891` as a no-op. The driver-bill mint gate (`loadStatusRequiresDeliveryDepartureStamp`, `delivery-evidence-status.ts:18`) fires on **both** `delivered_pending_docs` and `completed_docs_received` — the settlement-close predicate is strictly narrower than the mint predicate that feeds it. `appendSettlementLineFromDriverBillIfMissing` (`settlement-engine.ts:87`) is reachable from exactly 2 call sites, both gated behind the `delivered_pending_docs`-only close; the manual repair route (`pre-settlement.routes.ts:226`) is hard-blocked once `trip_closed_at` is stamped — **one-shot, no retry, ever.** L-0003 (has a settlement_line) hit that one-shot window with a bill already present, correctly. L-0002/L-0004 (zero lines) passed through it empty (L-0002: no bill existed yet at that instant, per DEFECT A; L-0004: 1 bill exists but post-dates the close) and `completed_docs_received` gave them no second chance. **L-0002 cannot self-heal** — both its delivery-evidence transitions are consumed and `completed_docs_received` is terminal (`load-state-machine.ts:66`); no remaining code path re-enters either the mint or the settle for it. **Fixes needed (not yet built, this pass was root-cause-only per explicit instruction "do not remint until the predicate is named"):** (a) re-read/refresh `load` after the C9-hold UPDATE in `bookLoad`, or include `driver_pay_rate_per_mile` in the INSERT's own column list (`:1658-1672`) — closes DEFECT A's still-open book-time instance; (b) add a `completed_docs_received` re-entry branch to `pingSettlementOnLoadEvent` that re-attempts `appendSettlementLineFromDriverBillIfMissing` against an already-closed settlement missing this load's line — closes DEFECT B, and is the only non-hand-write path to give L-0002/L-0004 a settlement line. | `apps/backend/src/dispatch/book-load.service.ts:1658-1672,1736,2173` (DEFECT A, stale `load` at book-time mint); | **REPORTED, not guessed (CC-1 2026-08-31, live Neon read, per LAW-BLAST-RADIUS-NO-VERTICAL-FIXES):** `FACTORING-BATCH-EXPECTED-ADVANCE-NOT-DISCOUNTED-FOR-PASS-THROUGH-FEES` — lead's INBOX assignment named `batch.service.ts:179-180`'s `0.95`/`0.025` literals as "three wrong values in one line (97.00% advance / 1.50% fee / 1.50% escrow), fix all three," citing a $120.00 wire-fee gap on a $95,075.00 batch. **Live-checked before touching code, per the never-guess law:** `factoring.factor` (table is singular, not `factors`) has exactly 2 active rows, both "Faro Factoring Full Recourse V1," both `advance_rate=0.9700, fee_rate=0.0150, reserve_rate=0.0150` — already correct, matching contract exactly ([[faro-factoring-contract-terms]]: Purchase Price = Net × (1 − fee − reserve) = Net × 0.97). `batch.service.ts:188-189`'s `0.95`/`0.025` are a **documented last-resort fallback** (existing comment: "Defaults 0.95/0.025 must NOT override the resolved factor's configured rates") that only fires if `getFactorForCustomer` fails to resolve a factor at all — for any real Faro-factored USMCA/TRANSP customer this path is dead code, not the live path the lead's dollar math implies. **The real, narrower gap:** `calculateBatchTotals` (`batch.service.ts:93-98`) computes only `expected_advance_cents = face × advance_rate` and `expected_fee_cents = face × fee_rate`; per the contract, `expected_advance_cents` (used by `bank-match.service.ts:57` to score-match against the actual incoming wire) should be **further discounted by "Transaction Fees" (wire fees, NSF, UCC, collection/attorney costs)** before it represents the amount actually wired — but the contract itself states these are **variable pass-through out-of-pockets, not a fixed fee** ("Purchase Price Proceeds = Purchase Price − Transaction Fees... Faro reimburses itself for"). **Did not implement a fix**: hardcoding "$10" (or the $120.00 observed on one batch) as a flat constant would contradict the contract's own language that this cost varies per transaction — that would be inventing a number, not fixing one. Flagging for the lead/owner: either (a) confirm a real fixed pass-through fee schedule exists somewhere I haven't found and point me at it, or (b) accept that `expected_advance_cents` is a pre-transaction-fee estimate by design and `bank-match.service.ts`'s match tolerance should absorb the gap instead. | `apps/backend/src/factoring/batch.service.ts:93-98,186-189`; `apps/backend/src/factoring/bank-match.service.ts:57`; `factoring.factor` table (2 rows, live-confirmed) | owner/lead — needs a real fee-schedule source or an explicit tolerance-band decision, not a coder guess | N/A until the above is answered | live Neon read of `factoring.factor` (2 rows, 97%/1.5%/1.5%, matches [[faro-factoring-contract-terms]] exactly); source read of `batch.service.ts`/`bank-match.service.ts`; contract terms memory cross-check | **REPORTED · advance/fee/reserve rates already correct live · the $120 gap is real but its dollar value is contractually variable, not a constant to hardcode** |

| **OPEN — money-adjacent, structurally silent (CC-3 2026-08-28, GO-0017 L3):** `DEPRECIATION-AUTOPOST-FK-VIOLATION-MASKED-BY-TICK-LEVEL-SUCCESS` — the L3 question was "is `accounting.depreciation_autopost` (last success 2026-08-01) inside its coded 62-day staleness window or a silent miss?" **Answer: BOTH.** Currently 27.5 of 62 days stale (`89280` min threshold, `health.routes.ts:342`) — the health check will not alarm for another ~34 days, so by the letter of the coded window this is "fine." But the deeper live read shows the health check is structurally blind to the actual failure, not just early: `accounting.depreciation_autopost_runs` for `run_date=2026-08-01` shows the ONE eligible asset that cron cycle processed (TRK, id `66d48635-…`) came back `outcome='error'`, `error_message="insert or update on table \"journal_entries\" violates foreign key constraint \"journal_entries_created_by_user_id_fkey\""` — the depreciation JE was never posted. **Root cause confirmed live:** `depreciation-autopost.cron.ts:15`'s `SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID` default is `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`; queried `identity.users` for that id — **zero rows**. Also queried the OTHER default UUID used everywhere else in the codebase (`00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`, e.g. `factoring-posting/default-interest.service.ts`, `fuel-posting/maybe-post-from-fuel-transaction.service.ts`, `recon-engine.service.ts`, `packet-assemble.service.ts`, `relay-wallet-bank-feed.service.ts` — `packet-assemble.service.ts`'s own comment calls this "the established SYSTEM_ACTOR_USER_ID convention") — **also zero rows in `identity.users`**, and zero `accounting.journal_entries.created_by_user_id` rows match EITHER placeholder ever, on all of prod. So this isn't only depreciation-autopost's bug in isolation; it is that no fallback system-actor user row exists at all, and depreciation-autopost is simply the one unattended cron that has actually hit a code path enforcing the FK against it. **Why the 62-day health check can never catch this, at any elapsed time:** `wrapBackgroundJobTick` (`background-jobs.ts:24-40`) marks the job "successful" (`recordBackgroundJobRun(jobName, true, null)`, which stamps `last_successful_run_at = now()`) as long as the outer `fn()` — `runDepreciationAutopostCronTick` — does not throw. But that function's own per-asset loop (`depreciation-autopost.cron.ts:160-169`) catches every per-asset error internally and only records it into `accounting.depreciation_autopost_runs`; it never re-throws. So the tick reports "successful" and resets the staleness clock to zero EVERY month, forever, regardless of how many (or all) assets error out inside it. The 62-day window is not "too generous" — it is measuring a signal (tick completion) that is decoupled from the thing that actually matters (did any asset's depreciation post). **Current live blast radius is small, not zero:** exactly 1 eligible fixed asset exists company-wide (`accounting.fixed_assets` filtered the same way the cron filters, live-queried) and its own `name` field is `"GUARD FA first-JE 2026-07-29"` — a guard/verification test fixture, $12,000 purchase price, not a real owner-purchased truck. | **DISPROVEN — query-back, not a defect (CC-3 2026-08-28, GO-0013):** hypothesis "USMCA's 92 open Samsara `identity_mismatch` findings block `dispatch.detention_evidence` / accessorial billing" — **NOT PROVEN, structurally cannot be true.** SOURCE-OF-TRUTH: `reconcileCap15IdentityForCompany` (`apps/backend/src/reconciliation/reconciliation-worker.service.ts:611-671`) vs `recordDetentionEvidence` (`apps/backend/src/dispatch/detention-approval.service.ts:142-187`). The two are structurally disjoint on every axis: (1) **different identity domain** — CAP-15 checks `mdata.drivers` ↔ `integrations.samsara_drivers` (by `samsara_driver_id`) and `mdata.vendors` (by `qbo_vendor_id`), i.e. DRIVER identity; detention evidence's only Samsara reference is `integrations.samsara_vehicles` joined by `local_unit_id` = `de.unit_id`, i.e. UNIT identity — no shared table, no shared key. | **★ OPEN (P1 · reverse-empty · systemic across 7 audit-report endpoints · CC-2 live-walk 2026-08-26)** `AUDIT-TRAIL-SUBJECT-LABEL-LOST-FOR-DEACTIVATED-ENTITIES` — **every `/reports/audit/*` endpoint silently loses the human-readable subject label ("Subject — not visible") for ANY historical event whose vendor/customer/driver/unit was LATER deactivated or voided — permanently, growing worse over time as more test/real entities get deactivated.** | `apps/backend/src/audit/audit-reports.routes.ts:65-120` (`auditSubjectJoins` — the shared LEFT JOIN helper reused by all ~7 sibling audit-report queries: activity-by-user, activity-by-module, financial-change-log, maintenance-decision-log, deduction-trail, void-reversal, period-close-history); live proof event `3e5cc896-63a5-43ee-8426-0976031e1e82` (vendor.created, 2026-08-16); `mdata.vendors` RLS policy `vendors_select` | B | **CC-2 (own /reports lane, non-money-classified backend file — not CC-1's territory)** | **Live-walked `/reports/audit/activity-by-user` (257 real records) per the standing hunt.** Noticed a recurring pattern: many rows across different subject types (vendor, customer, task, alert) show "Subject — not visible" instead of a real label. Ruled OUT as correct-by-design for `alert`/background-job rows (no matching CASE branch exists for `subject_type='alert'` — those are genuinely subject-less system/cron events, e.g. `recon.run_started`). But for `vendor.created` specifically: direct `GET /api/v1/audit/reports/activity-by-user` call returns `"subject_label": null` for event `3e5cc896-...` (2026-08-16 vendor.created) — yet a manual Neon query joining `mdata.vendors` on the exact same `id = subject_id AND operating_company_id = ...` condition (RLS-bypassed) resolves it immediately to `"CODEX-AUDIT-SPINE-VENDOR-20260816-0327"`. **Root cause, read directly from source, not guessed:** the vendor row has `deactivated_at: "2026-08-17T01:15:10.695Z"` (voided the day after creation, per CREATE-TEST-THEN-VOID) — and `mdata.vendors`'s own `vendors_select` RLS policy is `identity.is_lucia_bypass() OR (deactivated_at IS NULL AND operating_company_id IN (...))`. Since the audit query runs under a normal authenticated session (`withCurrentUser`, no bypass), RLS makes the deactivated vendor row **completely invisible to the LEFT JOIN itself** — not just filtered by a WHERE clause, but genuinely absent from the join's candidate rows — so the projection's `NULLIF(TRIM(audit_vendor.vendor_name), '')` has nothing to read and falls to NULL, rendering as the honest-looking "Subject — not visible" even though the vendor is NOT deleted (void-not-delete correctly preserved the row) and its name is fully available. **This is not limited to vendors** — `auditSubjectJoins` joins the identical pattern against `mdata.customers`, and near-identical patterns against `mdata.drivers`/`mdata.units`; any of those tables' RLS SELECT policies excluding inactive/deactivated/archived rows (a very common pattern in this codebase, confirmed for vendors) will silently blank the SAME class of historical audit rows. **Scope:** affects all ~7 sibling report endpoints reusing `auditSubjectJoins`/`auditSubjectProjection` (financial-change-log, maintenance-decision-log, deduction-trail, void-reversal-report, period-close-history, activity-by-module, activity-by-user), and will only get worse as more entities are voided pre-launch. **Fix shape:** add a narrow, read-only `SECURITY DEFINER` SQL function per entity type (e.g. `audit.resolve_vendor_label(vendor_id uuid, company_id uuid) RETURNS text`) that reads `vendor_name` bypassing RLS, scoped ONLY to the label column, callable from `auditSubjectProjection`'s CASE branches in place of the direct joined-column reference — preserves the existing company-scoped WHERE, requires no schema change to the base tables, and needs a migration only to create the function(s) (idempotent `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`). Did not build this myself in this block: a DB migration deserves the full local-Postgres rehearsal + idempotency-proof rigor this session's own migration-authoring standard requires, not a rushed same-turn fix; filing with the exact shape identified so the next block (mine or another seat's) can execute it properly. | — | OPEN |

next to it, so the button appears "half-broken" with a cryptic Postgres identifier surfaced to the operator instead of a real income line. **Fix shape (for whoever picks this up):** widen the CHECK succeed) — no application code change needed, Zod + frontend were already correct** |

an operator reading this 13-week forecast would simply never see money that other parts of the same app (Daily Prediction) correctly show as still coming. **Scope:** this affects every operating company with `CASH_FOLLOWS_ETA_ENABLED` on (confirmed at least 3 companies via `lib.feature_flag_overrides` earlier this session) and every proforma invoice whose raw delivery date has already elapsed by the time its ETA-adjusted cash date arrives — likely the common case for any invoice with nonzero net-terms/factoring lag, since the lag itself guarantees the projected date trails the delivery date. **Why not me:** the fix (importing `projectedCashDateSql` and conditionally branching on `CASH_FOLLOWS_ETA_ENABLED` inside `cash-forecast.routes.ts`, mirroring the already-proven pattern in `cash-flow.service.ts`) is a change to `apps/backend/src/accounting/`, which this GO-2237 paste explicitly reserves as CC-1's MONEY lane (multiple other seats are told "never steal CC-1 money/mint" in this same paste) — filing rather than fixing keeps this session's cross-lane-routing discipline consistent with that boundary. | — | **DONE · CC-1 2026-08-26 · `cash-forecast.routes.ts`'s proformaRes query now reuses `projectedCashDateSql` gated on `CASH_FOLLOWS_ETA_ENABLED`, matching `cash-flow.service.ts`'s own pattern; live-verified on invoice `INV-2026-00035`/load `L-20260811-0026`: old query returned 0 rows for the 13-week window, fixed query returns `{delivery_date: 2026-09-12, amount_cents: 100000}` (matches Daily Prediction's own $1,000.00 figure exactly); static guard `verify-acct-f9408-cash-forecast-proforma-eta-bucket.mjs` added (proven to fail on the pre-fix file, pass on the fix)** |

| **FIXED CODE THIS PR (CC-3 2026-08-23, live Fully-Wired-12 sweep on legal.contracts.send):** `LEGAL-F6250-SEND-CONTRACT-VARIABLE-INPUT-KEY-REMOUNT` — the Legal "Send Contract" wizard's step 3 ("Fill variables") rendered each variable row's `<div>` with `key={`${row.key}-${index}`}` — but `row.key` IS the live value of that same row's own "variable_name" text input. Every keystroke changed `row.key`, which changed the React key, which forced React to unmount the existing `<input>` DOM node and mount a brand-new one on every keystroke; the new node isn't focused, so only the very first character a user typed ever landed and everything after it was silently dropped with zero visible error. Live-reproduced via the real "Manual send" → Send Contract wizard on prod: typed "abc" into variable_name → field held only "a"; typed "x" then "y" as separate keystrokes → field held only "x". | **FIXED (CC-1 2026-08-22, PR #14345, SHA `356897ce6`, migration `202613080000` applied+verified on Neon):** `ACCT-F5901-FACTORING-CHARGEBACKS-FEES-ADVANCE-COLUMN-SHOWS-MEMO-TEXT-NOT-DOLLARS` — was: on `/factoring/chargebacks-fees` ("Chargebacks & Fees" tab), the **ADVANCE** column rendered the full free-text memo string (e.g. `"U6 6/6 -- TMS-internal factoring advance, real USMCA<->Faro FARO_FULL_RECOURSE_V1 agreement rates, reuse existing poster (INBOX-CC-1.md)"`) instead of a dollar amount — and the identical string ALSO renders in the neighboring **STATEMENT REF** column of the same row, i.e. both columns show the same text. The SAME invoice (`INV-2026-00038`, TC Freight LLC) correctly shows a real `Advance $1,794.50` on the sibling **Recourse Pipeline** tab, so the underlying dollar figure is intact — this is a display-layer defect, not corrupted data. Root cause pinned (Explore agent, source-read): `apps/frontend/src/pages/factoring/ChargebacksTable.tsx` — the `ChargebackFeeRow` type has no `advance_amount` field at all; its "Advance" column (~lines 49-58) binds `EntityLink` to `entityLabel(row.statement_reference, row.factoring_advance_id, "Advance")` — i.e. it was never wired to a dollar value, it renders the SAME `statement_reference` field the "Statement Ref" column (~lines 80-84) also renders verbatim. Compounding backend gap: `views.factoring_chargebacks_fees` (`db/migrations/202613010000_acct_f5760_factoring_chargebacks_fees_view_real_cents_columns.sql:34-49`) never selects `fa.advance_amount_cents` at all — unlike its sibling `views.factoring_recourse_at_risk` (`db/migrations/202612970000_acct_f5753_factoring_recourse_view_real_cents_columns.sql:71`, `(fa.advance_amount_cents::numeric / 100) AS advance_amount`), which correctly powers Recourse Pipeline's `$1,794.50`. Confirmed NOT data corruption: the seed script that created this exact row (`scripts/run-u6-factoring-advance-once.mts:162-189`) binds `advance_amount_cents` to a separately-computed real cents figure (`$7`), completely distinct from `notes`/`memo` (`$11`, the free-text string) — `accounting.factoring_advances.advance_amount_cents` for this row is correct and intact. | `apps/frontend/src/pages/factoring/ChargebacksTable.tsx` (Advance column ~L49-58, Statement Ref column ~L80-84); `db/migrations/202613010000_acct_f5760_factoring_chargebacks_fees_view_real_cents_columns.sql:34-49` (view missing `advance_amount_cents` select); reference pattern: `RecoursePipelineTable.tsx:97-100` (`fmtCurrency(row.advance_amount)`) | E | **CC-1 — money/GL/accounting lane, root cause fully pinned, fix not yet applied (CC-2 verify-live-never-build per role split)** | (1) Add `(fa.advance_amount_cents::numeric / 100) AS advance_amount` to `views.factoring_chargebacks_fees` via an additive `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` migration (mirror the `factoring_recourse_at_risk` pattern already proven). (2) Add `advance_amount: number` to `ChargebackFeeRow` in the frontend and rebind the "Advance" column to `fmtCurrency(row.advance_amount)` (mirror `RecoursePipelineTable.tsx`), leaving "Statement Ref" bound to `statement_reference` unchanged. (3) Live-Chrome re-verify `/factoring/chargebacks-fees` shows a real dollar figure distinct from Statement Ref. | Reproduced live via CDP port 9224 (screenshot + DOM text both capture identical strings in both columns); network trace confirmed endpoint `GET /api/v1/factoring/chargebacks-fees`; root cause confirmed via direct source read of both the frontend column binding and the backend view definition, plus confirmed the underlying `advance_amount_cents` DB value is NOT corrupted (ruled out via the seed script's INSERT parameter binding) | **FIXED — merged to main, PR #14345; migration 202613080000 rehearsed (ROLLBACK-wrapped, real row) then applied for real on Neon prod, fresh independent read after confirms advance_amount=1794.50 live; live-Chrome click-through is the natural next-deploy follow-up (frontend-only change, deploy-pending against the currently-live bundle)** |

| **FIXED (CC-1 2026-08-22, PR #14340, SHA `6084c2541`):** `SETL-F5900-SETTLEMENT-CLOSE-FOR-UPDATE-NULLABLE-OUTER-JOIN-500` — was: clicking **"Close settlement"** on `/driver-finance/settlement-close` threw a raw Postgres error, `FOR UPDATE cannot be applied to the nullable side of an outer join`, blocking 100% of load-bookended settlement closes. Root cause (CC-2, live-reproduced 2/2): `apps/backend/src/driver-finance/pre-settlement.routes.ts`'s `/settle` handler's row-lock query issued an unscoped `FOR UPDATE` spanning a `LEFT JOIN identity.users u` (nullable side). **Fixed by CC-1**: scoped the lock to `FOR UPDATE OF s` (the settlement row is the only one that needs locking; `d` is inner-joined and always has a row when `s` does; `u` stays correctly excluded). ## ★★★ STANDING RULE — THE COMPLETION REGISTER. EVERY FIXED FINDING IS TICKED BY THE CODER WHO FIXED IT.

**Owner-locked 2026-08-07 (Jorge, verbatim): _"create permanent rule that you will write all findings,
create list and checklist and each coder that works on it checks it once its done so I can also request
your list and you show it to me and I know the jobs were completed."_** Permanent. Applies to every lane.

**→ THE REGISTER IS `docs/audit/CC-3-FINDINGS-CHECKLIST.md`.** That file is what the owner reads to see what
is done. **This board holds the evidence and the fix instructions; the register holds the SIGN-OFF.**

1. **CC-3 files every finding in BOTH** — a row here (evidence + named lane + permanent-fix definition of
   done) and a `☐` row in the register, on the same commit. A finding that exists only in chat, a PR body,
   or CC-3's notes **is not filed**.
2. **THE CODER WHO FIXES IT TICKS ITS OWN ROW — never CC-3.** On merge, flip `☐` → `☑` and fill
   **Coder · PR · Date · Live proof · Guard (file + step #)**. CC-3 ticking another lane's box would destroy
   maker≠checker and make the register worthless.
3. **A TICK REQUIRES ALL FOUR PERMANENT-FIX CONDITIONS** (root cause at source · a **wired** CI guard that
   fails on the bug and passes on the fix · **live prod proof** · the class addressed). **Ticking without
   live proof is a false completion claim** and is treated as `fake-green` under the hardline rule. There is
   no "in progress" state — a half-fix in production is indistinguishable from no fix, so it stays `☐`.
4. **CC-3 RE-VERIFIES INDEPENDENTLY.** A tick is the coder's claim; CC-3 re-tests live and stamps
   `VERIFIED ✓` with its own evidence, or **reopens the row** stating what still fails. A row is closed only
   when both are present.

**Guard:** `scripts/verify-findings-register-signoff.mjs` (selftest **8/8**) asserts every OPEN board
finding has a register row, every `☑` carries its evidence cells, and no id is listed twice. Registered
`enforced` as `LAW-2026-08-07-FINDINGS-REGISTER-CODER-SIGNOFF`. **It is NOT yet wired into CI** — CC-3 has
no verify-step band (`CI-CC3-GUARDS-NEED-A-BANDED-ADOPTER`), so until a banded lane adopts it this rule is
**mandatory but not machine-enforced**. Stated plainly rather than left to a green registry to imply.

## ★★★ STANDING RULE — EVERY FINDING CARRIES A NAMED CODER AND A PERMANENT FIX. NO PATCHES.

**Owner-directed 2026-08-07 (Jorge, verbatim): _"write your findings in the shared file, instruct the
corresponding coder to permanently fix it. we do not want to have any more issues going forward."_**
This is permanent and applies to **every lane**, on **every row of this board**, from now on.

**A finding is not filed until the row states WHO fixes it and WHAT "fixed" means.** A row that describes a
defect without naming an owning lane is a complaint, not a work order — and a row that says "fix this"
without a definition of done invites a stopgap that reopens the same defect next month.

**Every OPEN row MUST carry all of:**

1. **AN OWNING LANE, named.** `CC-1` money / GL / WORM · `CC-2` GUARD (verify live, never build) ·
   mechanical / FE / backend. **Never route to the owner** — the owner is not a message bus
   (PERMANENT LAW §1). If a routing conflict exists, name BOTH candidate lanes in the row so the work is
   never stranded in a lane that does not build.
2. **THE ROOT CAUSE, located** — file and line where practical, with the live evidence that proves it.
   If the root cause is not proven, say **"UNVERIFIED — needs live check"** and say what is still unknown.
   **Never name a line you did not confirm executes.**
3. **A PERMANENT-FIX DEFINITION OF DONE**, per `docs/law/NEVER-GUESS-NEVER-DEFER-ALWAYS-VERIFY-ALWAYS-FIX.md`
   §4. All four, or the card does not close:
   - **ROOT CAUSE corrected at its source** — not the symptom, not the caller, not the display.
   - **A CI GUARD that FAILS on the bug and PASSES on the fix**, wired into `scripts/verify-steps/` so it
     actually runs. A guard that exists but is unwired enforces nothing.
   - **LIVE PROOF on prod.** CI-green is the floor. Merged is not done. Deployed is not done until the
     health SHA matches and the behaviour is observed.
   - **THE CLASS ADDRESSED** — if the same shape exists elsewhere, fix it or bound it explicitly with
     evidence. Never leave it implicit.

**FORBIDDEN AS A "FIX" — a card closed this way is reopened:** silencing or exempting the guard; widening a
constraint to turn red green; special-casing the one row that failed; editing the message instead of the
behaviour; reverting a correct change to dodge a check; or "fixing" a symptom whose root cause is unlocated.

**PREFER THE PERMANENT MECHANISM:** a DB constraint beats a guard, a guard beats a convention, a convention
beats a comment. **If a future writer can silently recreate the defect, it is not fixed.**

**Why this rule exists:** this repo has repeatedly shipped green checks over broken behaviour — a guard whose
matcher never examined the broken file, a UI promising a reversing entry it never posts, a banner reporting a
global default while the per-entity override said the opposite. Every one of those was green somewhere. The
definition of done above is what makes "fixed" mean fixed.

## ★★ STANDING RULE — QBO 2023–2025 FIGURES ARE STILL MOVING. DO NOT FILE NUMERIC DELTAS AS DEFECTS.

**Owner-stated 2026-08-07.** The internal accountant (**Martin**) is **still adjusting FY2023, FY2024 and
FY2025** in QuickBooks as a consequence of the **embezzlement by Ignacio Muñoz**. **Those figures will
keep changing until the reconciliation is complete.**

**WHAT THIS MEANS FOR EVERY LANE — this is a "do not file" rule, and it is not optional:**

1. **A numeric difference between QBO and TMS for FY2023–FY2025 is EXPECTED STATE, not a defect.** TMS
   cloned a snapshot; QBO has moved since and will move again. Filing the delta as a discrepancy is the
   `expected-state-recorded-as-failure` anti-pattern, and at these magnitudes it would send a lane
   chasing a number that is *supposed* to change.
2. **NEVER "fix" TMS to match a QBO figure from those years.** The locked strategy is
   **clone-as-is-then-adjust**: clone faithfully, then book post-opening adjusting entries — or let
   Martin fix it at source. Reaching in to force a match destroys the audit trail on both sides.
3. **NEVER write back to QBO.** Unchanged and absolute (`QBO_JE_PUSH_ENABLED` / `QBO_ENTITY_PUSH_ENABLED`
   default OFF). A lane "helpfully" correcting QBO would be corrupting the book of record **during an
   embezzlement reconciliation** — the one book that may be examined by counsel, a court, or an insurer.
4. **What IS legitimately reportable:** a **structural** defect that is true regardless of the numbers —
   a sign convention applied inconsistently, an account mapped to the wrong control account, a posting
   that never happens at all, a subledger that disagrees with its own GL **within TMS**. Those do not
   depend on Martin's figures and stay in scope.
5. **Record the number, do not act on it.** When a delta is measured, log it as a **tie-out input for
   when the close is finalised** — e.g. the **exact −$5,670.00** difference between the TMS opening entry
   and QBO's current A/R (battery item 65). That is useful; calling it a bug is not.

**CONTEXT THAT EXPLAINS THE CHART OF ACCOUNTS:** the A/R sub-accounts **"Unauthorized Expenses Ignacio
Muñoz" ($350,451.38)** and **"Unauthorized Expenses Anarely Alcazar" ($73,253.48)** on QBO's 12/31/2024
balance sheet are the embezzlement receivables. Per the locked decision they are **receivables pursued in
bankruptcy court — NOT written off and NOT reclassed to expense.** **No lane may "clean up" or reclassify
them.** They are evidence.

**WHEN THIS RULE EXPIRES:** when the owner states the 2023–2025 reconciliation is complete. Until then it
governs, and the opening JE stays deferred by owner decision — **which is an owner-written deferral, the
one form the never-defer law explicitly allows.**

## ★★★ PERMANENT LAW — owner-locked 2026-08-07 (supreme; supersedes nothing, binds everything)

> **WE NEVER GUESS. WE NEVER DEFER. WE ALWAYS VERIFY. WE ALWAYS FIX, NOT PATCH. WE WANT PERMANENT FIXES
> ALWAYS.** — owner, verbatim, 2026-08-07

**ENFORCED, not aspirational.** Canonical text: `docs/law/NEVER-GUESS-NEVER-DEFER-ALWAYS-VERIFY-ALWAYS-FIX.md`.
Guard: `scripts/verify-no-patch-or-defer-language.mjs`, wired at
`scripts/verify-steps/2703-verify-no-patch-or-defer-language.mjs`, registered `enforced` in
`docs/law/LAW.json` as `LAW-2026-08-07-NEVER-GUESS-NEVER-DEFER-ALWAYS-VERIFY-ALWAYS-FIX`. **Per
LAW-2026-08-05-B2 ("LAW = ENFORCED GUARD, OR IT IS NOT LAW"), writing this rule as prose alone would
itself have been a patch.** Live proof: guard `--selftest` **17/17 PASS**, repo scan **exit 0** across
**1,164** active work orders; `verify-law-registry` **exit 0** (44 laws, 38 enforced, every guard file
resolves).

**1. NEVER GUESS.** A fact requires evidence produced THIS SESSION from a PRIMARY source — the running
app, a live DB row, a job log, the file itself. Memory, a doc, a skill, another agent's "verified", and
inference from a similar case are not evidence. A `0` is not a verdict without the completeness
discriminator on the SAME table. **A passing guard is not proof the law it encodes holds — read what the
guard actually gates.** Cannot verify? The output is **"UNVERIFIED — needs live check"**, never a guess.

**2. NEVER DEFER.** The root problem is fixed in this change. No `TODO fix later`, no "ship now, fix
isolation later", no "CI green is enough". The ONLY allowed deferral is an owner-written tracker entry
with a future block id. If part of a scope is genuinely blocked, finish every other part IN FULL and say
plainly what is left and why — **silence about a gap is deferral.**

**3. ALWAYS VERIFY.** Done = real schema + local green + CI green + merged + **deploy verified live** +
behaviour confirmed on prod. **CI-green is the floor. Merged is not done. Deployed is not done until the
health SHA matches.** Strongest evidence, ascending: read it → create the row yourself and read it back →
**controlled before/after with a baseline captured first**. **Check before you file** — a finding that
dissolves on one more query was never a finding.

**4. ALWAYS FIX, NEVER PATCH.** Complete only when ALL hold: (a) root cause corrected **at its source**;
(b) a guard that **fails on the bug and passes on the fix**, wired via `scripts/verify-steps/NNNN-*.mjs`;
(c) **live proof on prod**; (d) **the class addressed** — same shape elsewhere is fixed or explicitly
bounded with evidence. **Forbidden as "fixes":** silencing a guard, widening a constraint to turn red
green, special-casing the row that failed, editing the message instead of the behaviour, reverting a
correct change to dodge a check, or "fixing" a symptom whose root cause you have not located.
**Prefer the permanent mechanism: a DB constraint beats a guard; a guard beats a convention; a convention
beats a comment.** If a future writer can silently recreate the defect, the fix is not permanent.
**When a correct fix turns something red, that redness IS the fix working — finish the work it points at,
do not silence it.**

### **OPEN · P3 · `LV-INSURANCE-POLICY-CREATE-NOT-IDEMPOTENT`** — a money-writing route is outside the idempotency middleware; bills are protected, POLICIES are not

**Owning lane: CC-1 (money controls — `middleware/idempotency.ts`).** Found by **CC-2** 2026-08-08 triaging the
never-in-CI FE guard sweep. **CC-2 did NOT edit money middleware.**

**CALIBRATED DELIBERATELY — my first read of this was worse than the truth.** `verify-insurance-module` reports
`insurance/policies` missing from `REQUIRED_MATCHERS`, and the route is
`POST /api/v1/insurance/policies/with-bills` → `createInsurancePolicyWithBills()` → `INSERT INTO
accounting.bills`. That reads like "a money route with no idempotency". **It is not that bad**, and the
difference matters:

**WHAT IS ALREADY PROTECTED (verified in `policy-create-atomic.service.ts`):** every bill is written with a
deterministic key `ins:{policyId}:{sequence}` and
`ON CONFLICT (operating_company_id, qbo_idempotency_key) … DO NOTHING`. **A retry cannot duplicate the bills
of a given policy** — the database prevents it.

**WHAT IS NOT PROTECTED (verified on prod `pg_constraint`):** `insurance.policy` carries **only**
`policy_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)` — **no unique constraint on `(operating_company_id, policy_number)`**. So a
retried POST mints a NEW policy id, whose bill keys (`ins:{newId}:…`) do not collide, and a second policy plus
a second bill schedule is created. The middleware would have caught that; the DB cannot.

**CURRENTLY UNREACHABLE, so it is P3 and not P1:** `insurance.policy` is **empty on prod — visible 0 ==
n_live_tup 0**, a real zero, consistent with `LV-TXN-014` (*insurance policy creation is a HARD 500 on every
entity*). Nobody can hit this path today. It becomes live the moment LV-TXN-014 is fixed.

**FIX — CC-1's call, two defensible options:** add `/^\/api\/v1\/insurance\/policies(\/|$)/i` to
`REQUIRED_MATCHERS`, and/or add a natural-key unique constraint on
`insurance.policy (operating_company_id, policy_number)` — the DB-level option is the stronger one, per
"a DB constraint beats a guard". **Sequence it with LV-TXN-014** so the control lands before the path opens.

**The guard is TRUE, not stale** — the 2nd of 20 sweep guards telling the truth (with `verify-dispatch-eta-columns`).
Its sibling assertion (`PolicyCreateModal.tsx` missing `selectedVendorId`) is untriaged and may be a separate
FE gap.

### **OPEN · P1 · `MIGRATION-NUMBER-RACE-IS-INTRA-LANE`** — the band guard cannot prevent it, because both colliding migrations came from the SAME lane's concurrent branches

**Owning lane: CC-3 (CI-guards) to build · CC-1 (me) diagnosed it and caused it.** Filed 2026-08-08.
**Read this before "fix" #1 gets built twice — I nearly filed the wrong fix myself.**

**WHAT HAPPENED.** `202612350000` was used by two migrations, both applied on prod, forcing the accepted
freeze in #4800 (`_driver_settlements_is_sample_data` 07:08:47Z, `_money_tables_audit_triggers` 07:55:13Z).

**THE OBVIOUS DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG.** A per-lane band guard already exists and already runs in the money gate —
`scripts/verify-migration-lane-band.mjs`: **`claude/` → HH 00–11, `cursor/`|`chore/`|`feat/`|`fix/` → HH
12–23**, disjoint by construction. My first theory was *"the three CC seats share the `claude/` band, so
subdivide it per seat."* **I checked before filing it, and it is wrong.**

**BOTH COLLIDING MIGRATIONS ARE CC-1'S OWN**, from two concurrently-open CC-1 branches:
`claude/settlement-sample-tag-202612350000` (this seat) and the branch behind **#4757 / ACCT-F178** (also
CC-1). Same lane, same seat, both in-band (`HH=00`). **A finer band — per seat or otherwise — would not have
prevented it**, because the two claimants were the same claimant at two different moments.

**THE ACTUAL MECHANISM: "next free" is computed against `origin/main`, and main is not the whole world.**
Each branch was cut at a different time, each correctly ran the documented check (*number strictly above
main's current max*, then `202612340000`), and each got `202612350000`. **Neither could see the other, because
the other was an unmerged branch.** The check is honest and still wrong, the same way the ACCT-F59 interlock
was honest and still wrong: **it asks a question about the past when the conflicting fact lives in the
present.**

**WHY VERIFY-STEPS DO NOT HAVE THIS BUG:** `scripts/verify-steps/CLAIMED-NUMBERS.json` reserves the number in
a file that must be **merged to main FIRST** (Rule 37, claim-before-author). The reservation is visible to
every other branch the moment it lands. **Migrations have no equivalent — there is nothing to collide with
until both files are already on main, i.e. until it is too late to renumber** (checksum freeze).

**FIX — the same shape that already works one directory over:**
**(a) RECOMMENDED — a migration claim registry**, `db/migrations/CLAIMED-MIGRATION-NUMBERS.json`, merged
before the migration file is authored, exactly mirroring `CLAIMED-NUMBERS.json` + Rule 37. Proven mechanism,
proven guard shape, no new concepts.
**(b) WEAKER — widen "next free" to consider OPEN BRANCHES/PRs**, not just `origin/main`
(`git ls-remote --heads` + the migration filenames on each). Catches more than main-only, but is racy by
nature and depends on remote state at check time. **Use (a).**

**DO NOT "FIX" IT BY:** subdividing the lane band (does not address a same-lane race — proven above), or
re-checking main's max harder at push time (main still cannot see an unmerged sibling branch).

**GUARD:** the registry's own claim-before-author check, mirroring `verify-verify-step-claimed-on-main.mjs`.
**Live proof:** two concurrently-open branches adding migrations cannot both pass the gate.

**COST IF NOT FIXED:** it recurs whenever one lane has two migration branches open at once — which is normal —
and each recurrence is **unfixable after the fact** (both files apply, renaming is forbidden by the checksum
freeze), so every one permanently consumes another frozen-baseline entry and another main-red until accepted.

### **OPEN · P0 · `REVREC-DOUBLE-RESIDUE-L-20260806-0008`** — the duplicate is **$1,875.50 TWICE OVER**: revenue AND A/R are both overstated. Reversal is PREPARED below; **owner posts it**

**Owning lane: CC-1 (money) to execute · OWNER to authorise.** Prepared by **CC-1** 2026-08-08.
**#4797 stops NEW occurrences. It does not repair this row — a code fix never revisits rows written before it.**

**★ THE HEADLINE NUMBER WAS UNDERSTATED. It is not one $1,875.50 error, it is two.** Reading all three
journal entries together (live, prod, USMCA, `bypass_rls='lucia'`):

| JE | date | entry | `reversed_by_je_id` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `7f2fff09-03e4-47d1-aafa-daba984127d2` | 2026-08-07 | **DR `1100` A/R 187550 / CR `4000` Freight Income 187550** — *"Invoice INV-2026-00006 posting"* | **NULL** |
| `f19cdf41-3bfe-4927-a0d3-6cbec90bf781` | 2026-08-08 | DR `1150` Unbilled 187550 / **CR `4000` Freight Income 187550** — Revrec Event 1 earn | NULL |
| `a5aa127d-61c2-4a47-b12a-ad3f6c242b1b` | 2026-08-08 | **DR `1100` A/R 187550** / CR `1150` Unbilled 187550 — Revrec Event 2 bill | NULL |

**Net effect on the ledger:**
- **`4000` Freight/Line-haul Income — credited TWICE = $3,751.00, should be $1,875.50 → OVERSTATED $1,875.50**
- **`1100` Accounts Receivable — debited TWICE = $3,751.00, should be $1,875.50 → OVERSTATED $1,875.50**
- `1150` Unbilled Revenue — DR (E1) then CR (E2), **nets to $0 — correct**, no repair needed

**So both a P&L account and a balance-sheet account are wrong by $1,875.50 each.** ACCT-F59's own error text
predicted exactly this — *"posting this invoice would credit revenue **and debit A/R** a second time"* — but
every report of this defect so far, including my own first pass, said only "revenue overstated". **The A/R
half was missed because the two debits sit in different JEs and only net out when you read all three
together.** An A/R aging or subledger tie-out will show `INV-2026-00006` twice over in the control account.

**PREPARED REVERSAL — reverse the INVOICE entry, not the latch.** ACCT-F59 rules the latch owns a delivered
load's revenue *and* A/R, so the invoice JE is the intruder. One balanced entry removes **both** duplicates:

```
REVERSE  JE 7f2fff09-03e4-47d1-aafa-daba984127d2   (Invoice INV-2026-00006 posting)
  DR  4000  Freight / Line-haul Income   187550
  CR  1100  Accounts Receivable (A/R)    187550
  memo: reverse duplicate invoice posting — load L-20260806-0008 revenue+A/R are owned by the
        DISP-01 two-event latch (ACCT-F59); see REVREC-DOUBLE-RESIDUE-L-20260806-0008
```

**After it posts:** `4000` = $1,875.50 (latch Event 1 only) · `1100` = $1,875.50 (latch Event 2 only) ·
`1150` = $0 — and GL A/R then ties to the `INV-2026-00006` subledger instead of doubling it.

**EXECUTION RULES — non-negotiable:** post through the **EXISTING** poster / void path (`reverses_je_id` +
`reversed_by_je_id` written both ways) — **no hand-SQL, and NO new GL math**. **Do NOT back-date it**: the
reversal's `entry_date` is a period decision and putting it in a closed period is its own defect. **Do NOT
delete or edit the original JE** — void-not-delete; all three entries stay on the books. Verified `NULL`
`reversed_by_je_id` on all three today, so **no reversal exists yet and this is not double-repair.**

**WHY IT IS NOT POSTED YET:** moving money in a live ledger is an owner action. **CC-1 has prepared it and
will execute on authorisation** — same standing as the other residue items.

**★ ONE RULING SHOULD COVER THE WHOLE PRE-FIX RESIDUE CLASS** — identical shape (code fixed forward, rows

### **OPEN · P1 · `LATCH-REVERSAL-NEVER-RELEASES-INTERLOCK`** — a reversed load is permanently blocked from re-recognition, and #4797 made the blockage wider

**Owning lane: CC-1 (money).** Found by **CC-1** 2026-08-08 while proving ACCT-F59 for the race fix.

`posting-engine.service.ts:236-241` states it against itself: *"Releasing the interlock is the LATCH's job:
`is_active` is the latch's own liveness flag… That reconciliation is tracked separately — **today a reversal
leaves the latch row active** (proven on prod: load `L-20260624-0083`'s two rows are still `status='posted'`,
`is_active=true` after their 2026-08-01 owner-authorized reversal)."*

**Consequence:** once a load's latch entry is reversed, the latch row stays `is_active=true`, so the invoice
poster keeps refusing forever — **the load can never be re-recognised by either path.** Revenue for it is
reversed and unrecoverable without a manual entry, which is precisely what "no hand-SQL" forbids.

**#4797 RAISES THIS RISK and that is stated deliberately.** Its second arm also refuses on
*load has reached delivery evidence*, which is a **permanent** property of a delivered load — so after a
reversal a delivered load is blocked by **both** arms, not just the stale latch row. **The fix is correct and
should ship; this card is the debt it makes more visible.**

**FIX:** the void/reversal path must set `is_active=false` on the load's
`accounting.load_revenue_recognition_postings` rows when their journal entry is reversed — releasing the
interlock as the code already says it should. **GUARD:** a `*.db.test.ts` asserting that after reversing a
latch JE, (a) its latch rows are `is_active=false` and (b) the load can be re-recognised. **Not a static
guard** — per `subledger-gl-tieout-ar.db.test.ts`, a static scan cannot prove a gate returned true or a row
landed. **Live proof:** `L-20260624-0083`'s two rows flipped to `is_active=false`, or an explicit owner
decision that they stay blocked.

### **OPEN · P0 · `ACCT-F59-INTERLOCK-IS-ONE-DIRECTIONAL`** — the double-revenue credit is a **473 ms race**, not an open design question; ACCT-F59 already rules who owns revenue

**Owning lane: CC-1 (money).** Found by **CC-1** 2026-08-08 while inventorying `CURSOR-RULING-DOUBLE-REVREC-INVOICE.md`.
**Read this BEFORE asking the owner "which side credits 4000" — that question is already answered in-repo.**

**1. THE DESIGN IS ALREADY RULED.** `apps/backend/src/accounting/__tests__/posting-engine-revrec-interlock.test.ts`
(**ACCT-F59**) states it verbatim: *"the invoice A/R poster **must refuse** a load-sourced invoice whose load
already carries an active DISP-01 revenue-recognition latch row… Run both over one load and revenue AND A/R
are both stated twice. On prod both flags are ON for TRANSP and USMCA (verified 2026-08-01), so this is a
**mechanism, not a style preference**."* **The latch owns the `4000` credit; the invoice must refuse.** That
also matches ASC 606 — revenue is earned at delivery, not at billing, and an invoice-side credit stamps the
**invoice date** rather than the delivery date, which is the date an auditor tests.

**2. IT DOUBLE-CREDITED ANYWAY, AND THE TIMING PROVES WHY (live, prod, `L-20260806-0008`):**

```
invoice row created   2026-08-07 02:05:48.506        (proforma, previous day)
invoice JE posted     2026-08-08 07:14:33.413711     <- income credited
latch earn JE posted  2026-08-08 07:14:33.886651     <- income credited AGAIN, 473 ms later
```

ACCT-F59's gate asks *"does this load already carry an active latch row?"* At `.413` the answer was
legitimately **NO** — the latch row did not exist until `.886`. **The interlock refused nothing because it
looked for a latch that had not happened yet.** It blocks invoice-after-latch and is **blind to
latch-after-invoice**.

**3. CAUSE IS STATEMENT ORDER IN ONE HANDLER** — `apps/backend/src/dispatch/loads.routes.ts`, same delivery
transition: `convertProformaToOfficial` (1334) → `sendDraftInvoice` (1340, posts income) → …
→ `latchOnDeliveryEvidence` (1368, posts income again). Invoice first, latch second, ~0.5 s apart — exactly
the observed gap.

**4. MEASURED IMPACT (live):** `4000 Freight/Line-haul Income` overstated **$1,875.50** on `L-20260806-0008`.
Full inventory of loads carrying latch rows: `L-20260624-0083` ($15,000, latch only — correct) and
`LUSMCAFREIGHT-20260806-0001` ($1.00, latch only — correct). **One load today — but it lands on EVERY
delivered-and-invoiced load once Gate B opens**, because that handler is the normal path.

**5. FIX — PREFER THE ORDER-INDEPENDENT ONE.**
**(a) Reorder** the handler so the latch runs first: smallest diff, but correctness then depends on statement
order and the next edit to that block silently reopens the defect. **(b) RECOMMENDED — the invoice poster
skips its income leg whenever `source_load_id` IS NOT NULL and the load is at or past a delivery-evidence
status, regardless of whether a latch row exists yet**; books `DR A/R / CR Unbilled`, leaving the latch as the
sole `4000` terminus. Cannot be reopened by reordering, and it is what the poster's own header already
prescribes (*"extend the invoice poster to skip income credit"*). **Manual (non-load) invoices keep crediting
`4000` directly** — no latch ever runs for them. **Write NO new GL math; reuse the existing poster.**

**6. GUARD — the invariant is RULING-INDEPENDENT, so it can be built before any decision:** *for any load,
`4000` is credited exactly once.* **Build it as a `*.db.test.ts`, NOT a static guard** — the reason is stated
on main in `subledger-gl-tieout-ar.db.test.ts`: *"A static scan can prove a poster is CALLED and correctly
ORDERED. It structurally cannot prove that a gate returned true, that a flag resolved ON, that the JE
balanced, or that a row landed."* A static guard would have been green through this entire defect.

**7. ⚠ DETECTION TRAP — DO NOT join on `source_transaction_type`.** The latch's postings carry
`source_transaction_type = NULL` and **structurally cannot carry it**: `CreateJournalEntryInput` /
`CreatePostingInput` in `journal-entries.service.ts` have no such field, so the latch records provenance via
`writeTransactionSourceLink` + `accounting.load_revenue_recognition_postings` instead. **Any census grouping
by `source_transaction_type` is blind to every latch posting** — which is precisely why `4000` looked like it
carried only `invoice` credits and the untyped rows were filed as a "minor data-quality note". Join through
`load_revenue_recognition_postings` instead. Also note `accounting.invoices` links loads via
**`source_load_id`**, not `load_id` — the obvious name does not exist.

**8. REPAIR of the existing $1,875.50** is a reversing entry through the **existing** poster, never
back-dated, never hand-SQL — **same "pre-fix residue" class as the $1,287.25 A/R and $33.40 A/P items. One
owner ruling should cover all three.**

**Status: OPEN — narrowed owner question is "confirm ACCT-F59 stands, approve fix (b)", NOT "which side owns revenue".**

### **OPEN · P0 · `CI-ACTIONS-DEAD-2026-08-08`** — no GitHub workflow has executed repo-wide since 02:39Z; "merge on green" is currently unsatisfiable for EVERY lane

**Owning lane: CI / infra (CC-3 CI-guards lane) + an OWNER BUSINESS DECISION if the cause is billing.**
Found by **CC-2** on 2026-08-08 while waiting for CI on #4771.

**MEASURED, not inferred.** `gh run list` — every run on every branch, **including pushes to `main`**, since
`2026-08-08T04:55Z` is a **nameless workflow at `path=BuildFailed`, `conclusion=startup_failure`, duration `0s`**.
The last **real** run of any workflow was `ci` at **`2026-08-08T02:39:25Z`** (branch `cc-2/driver-create-doc-upload`,
success, 21m17s). `gh run view` on the failures says *"This run likely failed because of a workflow file issue."*

**CONSEQUENCE — this is why it is P0, not housekeeping:**
`gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch <b>` returns **NOTHING** for `cursor/lv-txn-004-fe-status-wire` (#4769),
`chore/claim-reserve-2811-load-detail-names` (#4770), and `cc-2/lv-txn-002-guard-wired` (#4771). **All three merged
with zero CI runs**, and **#4769 (P2, the Kanban→money-aware status wire) is LIVE ON PRODUCTION having never been
verified by CI.** `gh pr checks` reports *"no checks reported"*, and because required checks never register, PRs
show **`mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`** — so the merge button is green precisely BECAUSE the gate is dead. Every lane's
standing order to "merge on green" is currently a no-op. This also silently voids `required-checks-gate`,
`hold-merge-gate` (the migration firewall) and `locked-guards` for anything merged in this window.

**RULED OUT (verified, not assumed):** no workflow file changed in the window — the last commit touching
`.github/workflows/` is `3ff4e8b37` (2026-08-07 01:04), ~24h before the outage, and CI ran green for hours after it.

**UNVERIFIED — most likely cause, needs a credential CC-2 does not have and will not grant itself:** an
account-level Actions limit (minutes / spending cap) on a **private repo owned by a personal account**. Supporting
signal: `gh api repos/tioperfumes07/IH35-TMS/rulesets` → **HTTP 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository
public to enable this feature"**, and `repos/...` reports `private=true`, `owner.type=User`.
`gh api users/tioperfumes07/settings/billing/actions` → **404 / needs the `user` OAuth scope**. CC-2 did **not**
run `gh auth refresh -s user` — widening a token's scope is an access-control change and is owner-only.

**WHAT THE OWNER MAY NEED TO DECIDE (state plainly, do not self-authorize):** if this is a billing/minutes cap,
restoring CI requires **paying for Actions minutes, raising the spending limit, upgrading the plan, or making the
repo public**. That is a business decision, not an engineering one.

**DO NOT "fix" THIS BY:** merging more PRs while `CLEAN` is meaningless, disabling required checks to match
reality, or re-characterising it as the harmless "ghost `BuildFailed` workflow" — that characterisation was
accurate earlier tonight but is **wrong now**, because there are no real runs left to sit alongside the ghost.

**ACCEPTANCE:** a real `ci` + `hold-merge-gate` run appears for a fresh PR and reports a conclusion; then
re-verify, on merged main, everything that merged blind in this window (#4769, #4770, #4771).

## ★★★ CC-3 DISPATCH — 2026-08-07 · COMPLETE + PERMANENT FIXES ONLY (no patches)

**OWNER RULE, BINDING ON EVERY ROW BELOW (CLAUDE.md §10):** *we never patch — we make complete and
permanent fixes.* A row is DONE only when **(1)** the root cause is fixed at its source, **(2)** a guard
exists that fails on the bug and passes on the fix, and **(3)** live proof is produced on prod. Green CI
is the floor, not the verdict. **Each row below also names THE PATCH THAT MUST NOT BE APPLIED** — for
most of these the tempting shallow fix makes CI green while leaving the defect, or is actively worse.

**★ ROUTING CORRECTION — READ FIRST.** Rows found by this lane were previously tagged `CC-2 / mechanical`.
**That is wrong per this board's own supreme law §3**, which says **CC-1 = money/GL/WORM · CC-3 =
mechanical/entity-scope/FE/CI-guards · CC-2 = GUARD, verify live, NEVER BUILD.** Routing build work to
CC-2 guarantees it is never built. **Mechanical/FE rows below are therefore addressed to the
MECHANICAL/FE lane (CC-3 role per §3), not CC-2.** This lane's current instance is the live verifier and
does not fix what it verified (maker != checker) — it owns CI-guards only.

### ORDER OF WORK — by blast radius, not by discovery order

**TIER 1 — MOVES CASH OR MISSTATES THE LEDGER (CC-1, money):**

1. **`LV-PAYABLE-SELECTOR-OFFERS-VOIDED-BILLS`** — voided bills are offered for payment in TWO
   independent pickers. **COMPLETE FIX:** every payable/open-bill query filters on the authoritative
   void column, and the status/void pairing is enforced **in the database** (CHECK or trigger) so no
   future writer can desync them. **DO NOT PATCH BY:** fixing only the one selector you found, or by
   back-filling `status` on today's rows — both leave the next writer free to recreate it.
   **PERMANENT because:** a DB constraint cannot be forgotten by a new code path.

2. **`LV-BILLPAY-VOID-NO-REVERSAL`** — void posts no reversing entry though the UI promises one.
   **COMPLETE FIX:** post the equal-and-opposite entry **through the existing poster** and write
   `reverses_je_id` / `reversed_by_je_id` both ways. **THE WORKING REFERENCE IS ALREADY IN-REPO** — the
   JE-void path does all of this correctly; copy it. **DO NOT PATCH BY:** writing new GL math, or by
   softening the UI text to stop promising a reversal — the promise is correct, the code is wrong.

3. **`LV-PAY-SETTLE-NOPOST`** — customer payments never post; A/R subledger vs GL control out by
   **$1,287.25** and growing. **COMPLETE FIX:** wire payment-received to the existing poster
   (DR selected deposit account / CR A/R), honouring the `Deposited to` selection, and reverse on void.
   **A/P is the working mirror — copy it.** **DO NOT PATCH BY:** a per-row "payments must post" check
   alone — **the guard must be the subledger-to-GL tie-out per control account**, because only the
   tie-out catches an invoice that reads `paid` against a GL still carrying it in full.

4. **`LV-REVREC-NOT-FIRING`** — cross-connection read-your-own-writes: `loads.routes.ts:1295` stamps
   `actual_departure_at` on connection A (uncommitted), `:1335` reads it on connection B via
   `withLuciaBypass`. **COMPLETE FIX:** fire the latch **after the transaction commits**.
   **DO NOT PATCH BY (this one is dangerous):** loosening the `missing_delivery_evidence` gate so the
   latch posts on status alone. That gate is CORRECT ASC-606 conservatism — loosening it starts
   recognising **unearned revenue**, which is worse than the bug. Also **do not** pass the route's
   `client` into the poster: it needs the `withLuciaBypass` RLS context.

5. **`LV-VOID-INVARIANT-BOTH-WAYS` + `LV-CANCEL-VOIDS-STATUS-ONLY` + `LV-AR/AP-OPEN-INCLUDES-VOIDED`** —
   **these are ONE root cause with four symptoms: void state is not authoritative anywhere in A/P.**
   **COMPLETE FIX:** one piece of work — enforce `status='void' <-> voided_at IS NOT NULL` in the DB,
   correct the cancel path to stamp both, and make every open-balance aggregate exclude voided rows.
   **DO NOT PATCH BY:** fixing the four cards separately, or by a one-directional guard — the pairing
   is broken in BOTH directions (invoices: status set / timestamp missing; bills: timestamp set /
   status missing), so a one-sided assertion passes on half the corrupt rows.
   **TRAP:** `accounting.bill_payments` uses **`revoked_at`**, not `voided_at`; `vendor_credit_applications`
   uses `voided_reason`, invoices use `void_reason`. **A copy-paste fix WILL silently miss tables — you
   need a per-table map.**

6. **`LV-BANK-TWO-SIGN-CONVENTIONS`** — one column, two conventions (Relay Fuel Wallet positive, all
   else negative). **COMPLETE FIX:** normalise on write so `amount_cents` is a true magnitude with
   `is_credit` the sole direction carrier — which is the law two files already declare — or record the
   convention per account in the schema. **DO NOT PATCH BY:** special-casing Relay in each reader; that
   multiplies the trap. **VERIFY FIRST, DO NOT ASSUME:** whether the live recon engine actually
   mis-matches is UNVERIFIED — its comment is false for 96% of credits, but both sides may normalise
   identically and cancel. Trace the QBO side before changing behaviour.

7. **`LV-BANK-BANNER-SAYS-FLAG-OFF`** — the banking page tells operators categorize does not post; the
   flag is **ON for all three entities** and it does. **COMPLETE FIX:** render the **live per-entity
   override**, never the global default. **DO NOT PATCH BY:** editing the sentence to say "ON" — static
   copy asserting a flag state will rot again the moment the flag flips.

**TIER 2 — MECHANICAL / FE (mechanical lane per §3 — NOT CC-2):**

8. **FIXED on main (verified 2026-08-10)** `LV-LOAD-DETAIL-SHOWS-UNASSIGNED` — `GET /dispatch/loads/:id` now projects `assigned_primary_driver_name`, `assigned_unit_number`, and `trip_type` from `mdata.drivers`, `mdata.units`, and `mdata.loads` respectively, entity-scoped. The drawer no longer shows "Unassigned"/"-" for loads that have a primary driver, unit, or trip type. The UI does not fall back to a UUID.

9. **`LV-STOP-ZIP-DROPPED`** — `postal_code` is NULL on **0 of 18** stops while city/state persist.
   **COMPLETE FIX:** persist it on the booking path. **WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC:** it is the PC*MILER
   routing key — without it, per-mile driver pay and IFTA jurisdiction miles are unreachable.

10. **`LV-DISPATCH-TOAST-LIES`** — "Load booked and dispatched" after an audited DOT override, while the
    load never left `assigned_not_dispatched`. **COMPLETE FIX:** report the status the SERVER returned.
    **An override audit trail attesting to an action that did not happen is worse than no override.**

11. **`LV-BULK-DELIVER-NOLATCH`** — bulk "Mark delivered" stamps delivery evidence and never latches.
    **COMPLETE FIX:** call the latch — **using item 40's after-commit ordering**, or you reproduce the
    Tier-1 #4 timing bug in a second place. **Note:** the widened guard on this branch is *correctly RED*
    on that file and cannot go green until this is done. That redness is the forcing function, not a
    problem to silence.

12. **`LV-EXPENSE-VOID-UNREACHABLE`** — the void endpoint exists, no UI reaches it, and the FE renders a
    `void` badge it can never produce. **COMPLETE FIX:** either surface the endpoint on the expense
    detail page, **or** state the read-only decision explicitly and remove the dead badge branch.
    **Either answer is fine; the current ambiguous state is the one that is not.**

13. **`SKILL-DRIFT-USMCA-HIDDEN`** — two AUTO-LOADED skills say USMCA is hidden/future with 0 balances;
    prod and this lane's live transactions disprove it. **COMPLETE FIX:** correct the skill text AND add
    a presence-ratchet so no auto-loaded skill can describe USMCA as hidden again. **DO NOT PATCH BY:**
    editing the prose only — an unguarded doc fact drifts back.

**TIER 3 — OWNED BY WHOEVER OWNS THE BLOCK:**

14. **`BLOCK-0280-02-BOILERPLATE-ACCEPTANCE`** — the abolished-hold half is **DONE** (removed at the root

## §2-D NOTE (do not let this class come back)

The Layer-D test is the **inline +Create inside a picker/wizard** — it must be **exercised** (click, fill, save,
confirm the row persists to the canonical table and appears selected, with NO native GET). It is NOT satisfied by:

- "the code is wired to POST" — the Book Load customer create *was* wired to `createCustomer()`, but a nested
  `<form>` HTML5-drop meant the POST never fired. Code inspection is the exact false signal.
- a `created_at` row from a **module-level** create modal — that proves the module create works, not the
  inline-picker create. They are different code paths (the module modal is not inside a wizard `<form>`).

Until an inline +Create is actually exercised and confirmed to persist, its row is `UNVERIFIED`, never `PASS`.

## The gate

Only **GUARD** writes `VERIFIED`, after independent live re-check (git for code, Neon for data, the app for UI).
Governed by `docs/audit/AUDIT-LAW-PERMANENT.md` (order C→B→A→D→E; a screenshot is not a Layer-E pass; "complete"
= 30/30 certified only).

| **★ CARDS REFUTED** `LV-WF064-ALIVE` — **the WF064 / dispatch outbox lifecycle WORKS: producer AND consumer both fire** | — | C | **evidence for the two WF064 cards below — CC-1/CC-3 should STOP building against them** | **LIVE-PROVEN 2026-08-06 (CC-3 live-verifier lane) on deploy `e6343f4`, USMCA.** Two board cards state this lifecycle is dead: *"the whole WF064 lifecycle is inert end-to-end — wired, never executed"*, *"0 of 31,646 outbox events match `dispatch.*` / `%wf064%`"*, *"WF064-consumer dead (P1) … the settlement cycle never fires."* **All of that is a misreading of an empty queue.** I booked and dispatched ONE load through the real Book Load wizard (`L-20260806-0005`, `a0b1df25-e49e-4853-b8ee-a26b407e88ba`, USMCA) and **both events fired and were CONSUMED**: `dispatch.load.dispatched` created `17:02:41.402Z` → **`delivered_at 17:02:46.213Z`**, `retry_count 0`, `failed_at NULL`; `dispatch.wf064.override_notice` created `17:02:41.402Z` → **`delivered_at 17:03:10.184Z`**, `retry_count 1`, `failed_at NULL`. `dispatch.*` total **0 → 2**, `%wf064%` total **0 → 1**. **CORRECT CONCLUSION: the lifecycle was never EXERCISED, not broken** — no load had ever been dispatched in the TMS, so nothing had ever produced the event. The prior 0-count was accurate as a measurement and wrong as a verdict. This is the `expected-state-recorded-as-failure` anti-pattern applied to an event stream: an empty queue on a system that has never performed the triggering action is EXPECTED STATE. **ACTION: close the two WF064 cards as not-a-defect / never-exercised. Do NOT spend coder time "reconnecting" a consumer that demonstrably delivers.** Note the earlier GUARD correction was right that `n_tup_ins = 0` on `escrow_deductions_pending` is conclusive that no deduction ever landed — but that too follows from never having dispatched, and is not evidence of a broken consumer. Full record: `docs/audit/LIVE-TXN-BATTERY-2026-08-06.md` item 10b. | — | **EVIDENCE — refutes the 2 WF064 cards; no build required** |
| **FIXED (PR #8215)** `LV-OUTBOX-ERRCOL` — **outbox writes SUCCESS detail into `last_error`, destroying the real failure message** | — | C | **CC-3 / mechanical** | **LIVE-PROVEN 2026-08-06 (CC-3 live-verifier lane) on deploy `e6343f4`.** Both successfully-delivered dispatch outbox rows carry a **success** string in the **`last_error`** column: `dispatch.load.dispatched` → `last_error = 'driver_instructions_distributed'`; `dispatch.wf064.override_notice` → `last_error = 'override_notice_delivered_to_3_owner(s)'`. Both have `delivered_at NOT NULL` and `failed_at NULL`, i.e. they are healthy. **Two consequences.** (1) Any triage query of the shape `WHERE last_error IS NOT NULL` returns **healthy** rows, so the column cannot be used to find failures — it silently inverts the meaning of the operator's most obvious query. (2) **Worse and concrete:** the override-notice row has **`retry_count = 1`**, so its first delivery attempt genuinely DID fail — and that real error text has been **overwritten by the later success string and is now unrecoverable**. The one row that could have told us why a WF064 notice failed has had its diagnosis destroyed by the success path. **FIX REQUIREMENT:** stop writing success detail to `last_error`. Put delivery outcome/detail in its own column (e.g. `last_result` / `delivery_note`) and leave `last_error` populated **only** on a failed attempt, never cleared or overwritten by a subsequent success — or append attempt history rather than overwriting, consistent with the append-only/WORM posture (§2). **STANDARD:** a failure-diagnosis column is write-on-failure-only; overwriting it on success is the observability equivalent of deleting the audit row. **GUARD:** assert no success path writes `last_error`, and that a retried-then-delivered row retains its original failure text. Must be `--selftest`ed and mutation-proven. **Recorded by the live-verifier lane, which does not build.** Full record: `docs/audit/LIVE-TXN-BATTERY-2026-08-06.md` item 10c. | — **★ PERMANENT FIX REQUIRED — owner directive 2026-08-07 (Jorge: "instruct the corresponding coder to permanently fix it; we do not want to have any more issues going forward"). Collision prevention is the `CLAIMED-NUMBERS.json` registry; the mod-4 band is a secondary convention for prefix-matched lanes. **Recording the correction because a wrong blocker sends the next lane re-cutting bands that do not need re-cutting.** **WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED — small, concrete, no policy change:** two guard scripts exist on `origin/main`, both self-test green, both currently ORPHANED (baseline-exempted with a stated reason in `scripts/.guard-exempt.json`, so they run in NO CI step and enforce NOTHING): **(a)** `scripts/verify-no-patch-or-defer-language.mjs` — selftest **17/17**; enforces owner LAW-2026-08-07 (NEVER GUESS · NEVER DEFER · ALWAYS VERIFY · ALWAYS FIX). Prod result: `review_state=matched`, `matched_journal_entry_id` SET, **new JE `ff746cfa` created at 15:13:10 (same second as the bank row updated_at), memo `Bank categorization cb271ba0-… posting`, debits $918.00**, and USMCA `accounting.journal_entries` **27 → 28**. A new balanced JE, whose own memo says it came from the categorize. **THE FLAG IS ON — the POSTER is correct, the BANNER is wrong.** `lib.feature_flag_overrides`: global `default_enabled=false`, but per-entity **TRUE for USMCA, TRANSP and TRK** — enabled everywhere. **ROOT CAUSE — hardcoded prose, not a scoping bug:** `apps/frontend/src/pages/banking/components/BankingTransactionsDesignView.tsx:2155-2157` is a static `<p>`; the words "stays OFF by default" and "does not post a balanced TMS JE" are literals. **The banner never reads the flag it names.** This is the exact masked-scope error the standards call out — reading global `default_enabled=false` and concluding OFF instead of resolving the per-entity override. **WHY P0 (worse than the other UI-truth defects filed today):** those misinform; **this one changes the books when acted on.** 110 transactions remain in the for-review queue; an operator trusting the banner posts 110 unintended journal entries into a live GL during a Ch.11 case with an active embezzlement reconciliation, where every entry is potential evidence. **NOTE FOR THE REVIEWER:** the same banner correctly warns that `matched_journal_entry_id` "is not proof that bank-feed GL posting is live" — a true caution that could lead someone to dismiss this evidence. I did NOT stop at the linkage column: the NEW JE row, its creation timestamp, its memo, its balanced debit and the 27→28 entity count are all confirmed. **FIX COMPLETELY:** render the sentence from `resolveFlagEnabled(BANK_FEED_GL_POSTING_ENABLED, operating_company_id)`; when posting is ON, say so loudly ("Categorizing WILL post a balanced journal entry for this entity"). **Never print a flag global default as the effective state.** **Guard: assert the banner text is derived from the resolved per-entity flag and that no literal "stays OFF" string remains in the component.** Detail: `docs/audit/LIVE-TXN-BATTERY-2026-08-06.md` item 82. | **FIXED · OWNER-GATED=no** |
