I confirmed that UUID **IS** the bank transaction id — so reverse drill works **by parsing prose**. The JE's structured columns are `source='auto'`, `source_system='tms'`, which identify no record. **Meanwhile `banking.bank_transaction_splits` — which carries `result_journal_entry_id` plus `load_id`/`driver_id`/`unit_id`/`trailer_id`/`vendor_id`/`customer_id`/`item_id`/`posting_status`/`voided_at` — holds 0 rows** (`visible_all` 0 == `n_live_tup` 0, discriminator satisfied). The purpose-built mechanism is unused. **WHY IT MATTERS:** LAW §10a requires forward AND reverse drill-through. The reverse direction is load-bearing on a free-text string with no FK, no constraint, no index. Any memo edit or template change silently severs the audit path from a ledger entry back to the bank line that produced it — the exact path an examiner walks. **It works now and would break quietly.** **NOT CLAIMED / UNVERIFIED:** the JE-detail UI reverse drill ("Source maps bank_categorization → Banking Transactions", documented at `BankingTransactionsDesignView.tsx:1530`) is a MODULE-level jump, not row-level, and I have not exercised it. **FIX:** write the `bank_transaction_splits` row the schema was designed for, or add `source_bank_transaction_id` to `accounting.journal_entries`. Either turns the reverse link into a constraint instead of a sentence. **Guard: assert every JE whose memo begins "Bank categorization" has a structured FK back to its bank transaction.** Detail: `docs/audit/LIVE-TXN-BATTERY-2026-08-06.md` item 83. | **FIXED · OWNER-GATED=no** |
| **★ OPEN (P0 · legal evidence) — HEADLINE CORRECTED, read the CC-3 SELF-CORRECTION below before building** `LV-MONEY-TABLES-HAVE-NO-AUDIT-TRIGGER` — **123 of 134 money tables have NO audit trigger (41% of rows unaudited), INCLUDING `accounting.journal_entry_postings` — the ledger header is audited, the debits and credits are not** | — | C | **CC-1 (WORM / audit integrity)** | **MEASURED on prod from `pg_trigger`/`pg_proc`/`pg_stat_all_tables`, `current_user` asserted.** Schemas `accounting`+`driver_finance`+`banking`: **134 tables · 11 WITH an audit trigger · 123 WITHOUT (92%) · 46 of those hold live data · 140,248 of 343,195 rows unaudited (41%)**. **HEADLINE:** `accounting.journal_entries` (header) has **1** audit trigger; **`accounting.journal_entry_postings` — every debit, credit, account and amount — has ZERO.** An entry's existence is audited; **its money is not.** A posting's amount or account can be altered with no `audit.row_changes` record while the header's audit row reads as if nothing changed. For a double-entry system that is the wrong half to protect. **Also unaudited, holding real data:** `expense_lines` 33,980 · `expenses` 27,072 · `invoice_lines` 21,213 · `posting_batches` 14,922 · `payment_applications` 12,209 · **`payments` 12,127** · `journal_entry_postings` 3,635 · `transaction_source_links` 3,614 · `periods` 120 · `chart_of_accounts_roles` 131 · `driver_pay_rates` 93. **PROOF THE GAP IS ALREADY LOSING HISTORY:** `driver_finance.driver_settlements` `n_tup_del=7` and `driver_settlement_deductions` `n_tup_del=14` — both with 0 audit triggers, and NEITHER appears among the 27 DELETEs recorded in `audit.row_changes` (item 78, all `mdata.*`/`maintenance.*`). **21 driver-pay records were hard deleted and the audit trail does not know they existed.** `driver_settlements` HAS a `voided_at` column, so void-not-delete was available and unused. This is what a driver was PAID and what was DEDUCTED — a driver dispute or a labour/tax authority would find no record of either the row or its removal. **COMPOUNDS WITH `LV-AUDIT-TRAIL-HAS-NO-ACTOR`:** that card proved 2 of 2,319,894 audit rows name a user, 0 name a role or session. Together: **92% of money tables produce no audit record at all, and the 8% that do cannot say who made the change.** "We have a WORM audit trail" is not a safe summary of this system. **WHY P0:** the repo states it holds "live financial and legal-evidence data" and §2 requires append-only audit on every table. Confirmed Ch.11, active Muñoz embezzlement litigation with the Unauthorized Expenses receivables held AS evidence. An embezzlement case is fought over WHO changed WHICH number WHEN — on 41% of rows and on every GL posting line, this system cannot answer. **NOT CLAIMED:** no evidence of malicious alteration; the 21 deletions are most plausibly test-data cleanup (Rule 4 — all TMS-native data is test). **The finding is the missing capability, not an accusation** — and establishing intent would require the very trail that is absent, which is the point. **FIX THE CLASS, not two tables:** attach the existing `audit.row_changes` trigger to every transactional table in these schemas, starting with `journal_entry_postings`, `payments`, `payment_applications`, `expenses`, `expense_lines`, `invoice_lines` and the `driver_finance` settlement family; pair with the actor fix from `LV-AUDIT-TRAIL-HAS-NO-ACTOR` (a row recording neither the change nor the author is not evidence). **Guard: assert every transactional table in accounting/driver_finance/banking has an audit trigger, so a new money table cannot ship unaudited.**  **★★ CC-3 SELF-CORRECTION 2026-08-07 (battery item 88) — THE HEADLINE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. DO NOT BUILD FROM IT.** I claimed `accounting.journal_entry_postings` is "unprotected" because it has no AUDIT trigger. **It has THREE** — `ensure_journal_entry_balanced` (a DB-LEVEL guarantee every entry balances, which is WHY item 84 measured 0 unbalanced entries), `trg_block_closed_period_journal_entry_postings`, and `refuse_financial_row_delete`. `expense_lines` has FOUR. **"No audit trigger" is NOT "no protection" — I used a proxy metric and it was invalid.** **`hos.duty_status_events` is EXEMPLARY and is the model to copy:** blocking triggers on UPDATE and DELETE, `ih35_app` holds NO upd/del grant, `n_tup_upd=0` / `n_tup_del=0` across **630,626** inserts — append-only ENFORCED, not asserted. **THE REAL FINDING SURVIVES, in two precise parts.** **(1) WORM DELETION IS SCOPED TO ONE ROLE AND SILENTLY PERMITS EVERY OTHER.** `accounting.refuse_financial_row_delete()` opens: `IF current_user <> 'ih35_app' THEN RETURN OLD; END IF;` — the guard fires ONLY for the app role, so `neondb_owner`, a migration, a maintenance script or a console session deletes financial rows with **no block and no error**. **That is exactly how `driver_settlements` took 7 deletions and `driver_settlement_deductions` 14 WHILE CARRYING THIS VERY TRIGGER** — the puzzle in the original card, now solved. Those tables also have no audit trigger, so **nothing recorded it**. A break-glass path for administrative repair is defensible; a **silent, unlogged** one is indistinguishable from tampering after the fact. **(2) MUTATION IS NEITHER BLOCKED NOR RECORDED.** `accounting.payments` has taken **72,824** updates and `accounting.expense_lines` **305,542**, neither with an audit trigger. Deletion is the protected verb; **mutation is not** — and quietly changing an amount is at least as damaging as deleting a row. **REVISED FIX (supersedes the fix above):** (a) make `refuse_financial_row_delete` refuse for **ALL** roles, with an explicit **LOGGED** break-glass path if administrative deletion must exist; (b) attach the audit trigger to the transactional money tables so MUTATIONS are recorded; (c) copy the `hos` block-don't-just-record pattern wherever append-only is claimed. **Guard: assert no financial table grants a silent delete escape by role.** Detail: `docs/audit/LIVE-TXN-BATTERY-2026-08-06.md` item 87. | **FIXED · OWNER-GATED=no** |
| **LAW — PERMANENT, ENFORCED** `LAW-2026-08-07-VERTICAL-METHOD` — **work is drained VERTICALLY by CLASS, globally and universally. NEVER module-by-module. NEVER the old block way.** | — | C | **ALL LANES** | Owner rule, made permanent and ENFORCED 2026-08-07 after a lane reverted to module-by-module work. **It was already written in all four lane standing orders and that was not enough** — prose is followed exactly as long as someone remembers it, and PERMANENT LAW §2 says *law = enforced guard, or it is not law*. Now registered as `LAW-2026-08-07-VERTICAL-METHOD` in `docs/law/LAW.json` with guard `scripts/verify-vertical-method-law-present.mjs`, wired into verify-step 2733. **THE METHOD:** (1) pick a defect CLASS, never a module; (2) sweep it GLOBALLY — every instance in the repo AND on prod, MEASURED not estimated; (3) classify ORIGIN before calling any gap a defect, because imported rows are expected state and "fixing" them invents financial data; (4) fix the ROOT CAUSE once, in ONE PR, for every instance (§9.0.17: ≥3 identical sites = one sweep, never per-site PRs); (5) ship ONE mutation-proven ratcheting guard — plant defect = RED, restore = GREEN; (6) a class is drained ONLY at zero live instances AND a guard that exists; (7) modules certify LAST, from drained classes, never the reverse. **The guard is a PRESENCE ratchet and deliberately does not judge whether a given PR is vertical** — that is judgment, and judgment rules stay judgment rather than being force-guarded into noise. What it makes impossible is a lane quietly deleting the method from its own operating order. | LAW.json | — |

| **★ OPEN (P1 · money · WORM)** `LV-ESCROW-SUBLEDGER-NOT-WORM` — **the driver-facing escrow subledger and the settlement earnings lines are HARD-DELETABLE by the runtime role with ZERO audit trail, while their GL counterparts are protected — the DB permits exactly the "split-brain" the escrow code refuses to create** | — | C | **CC-1 (money / GL / WORM)** — the fix is a migration (financial cluster) | **MEASURED LIVE on Neon prod `br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a`, not inferred from migrations.** Single query, `has_table_privilege('ih35_app', tbl, 'DELETE')` + `pg_trigger` (`tgtype & 8`) + audit-trigger presence, all in one statement so the same run carries its own positive control. **UNPROTECTED — `ih35_app_can_delete = TRUE`, `delete_triggers = 0`, `audit_row_trigger = 0` on all four:** `driver_finance.escrow_ledger` (the held-in-trust driver escrow subledger), `driver_finance.escrow_balances` (the driver's running balance), `driver_finance.escrow_deductions_pending`, `driver_finance.settlement_lines` (driver earnings — which this repo's OWN `docs/audit/void-predicate-map.json` classifies as *"transactional money and `is_active` IS its void marker"*, so a void marker exists and nothing forces its use). **POSITIVE CONTROL in the same result set — the protection mechanism is real and detectable where it is applied:** `accounting.escrow_postings` (`trg_no_delete_escrow_postings`, no DELETE grant), `accounting.journal_entry_postings` (3 delete triggers, no grant), `accounting.bill_payments` (2 triggers, no grant), `accounting.escrow_accounts` (no grant). **THE DECLARED STANDARD, read from prod:** exactly **9** tables carry `trg_worm_refuse_delete` — `accounting.bill_lines/bill_payments/bills/expense_lines/journal_entry_postings/payment_applications`, `banking.bank_transactions`, `driver_finance.driver_settlements`, `driver_finance.driver_settlement_deductions`. The four above are **outliers inside a protected neighbourhood**, not an un-started programme. **THE ASYMMETRY IS INTERNAL TO ESCROW AND IS THE POINT:** the GL side of escrow is WORM; the driver-facing side is not. `apps/backend/src/driver-finance/escrow-forfeit.service.ts:182` explicitly refuses a *"split-brain forfeit (accounting posted without driver-facing decrement)"* — **the database allows that identical split-brain to be produced by a DELETE.** Escrow is money held in trust and returned 60–90d post-separation (locked decision, escrow = LIABILITY, GL `2100 Driver Escrow - Held in Trust`, `system_purpose='driver_escrow_liability'`, USMCA target $2,500 active); a deleted `escrow_ledger` row silently changes what the company owes a driver and is precisely the record a driver suit, an auditor or counsel would demand. **PRECEDENT THAT THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL:** `pg_stat_user_tables` on prod shows `driver_finance.driver_settlement_deductions` `n_tup_ins=14 / n_tup_del=14 / n_live_tup=0` and `driver_settlements` `n_tup_ins=12 / n_tup_del=7` — financial rows **have** been hard-deleted on this database. **NOTE FOR THE FIX, verified from the function body:** `accounting.refuse_financial_row_delete()` refuses **only when `current_user = 'ih35_app'`** and `RETURN OLD` (i.e. ALLOWS the delete) for every other role — so `neondb_owner`, which this MCP itself intermittently runs as, is not covered by the trigger on ANY of the 9. Grant-revocation is the layer that actually holds; the two `driver_finance.*` tables that carry the trigger still have `ih35_app_can_delete = TRUE`, so the trigger is their ONLY layer. **FIX REQUIREMENT:** extend both layers to the four tables — `REVOKE DELETE ... Proof of the gap: `SELECT COALESCE(is_dispatch_blocked,false) FROM mdata.drivers` in `dispatch/auth-gates/wf-038-active-driver.gate.ts` passed this guard at exit 0, while `is_dispatch_blocked` exists ONLY on `mdata.units` (prod-verified: 0 of 89 columns on `mdata.drivers`, 1 of 69 on `mdata.units`). Because `checkGates` does not catch, that throw propagated out of the `auth-gates` preHandler and **every dispatch mutation carrying a driver_uuid 500'd before reaching its handler** — quick-assign, PATCH assignment and book-load: no driver could be attached to any load. FIX (fix-once-lands-everywhere): new paren-depth-aware `extractSelectList` + `unqualifiedSelectListColumns` passes in the shared guard, so all ~4,100 SQL blocks in the repo are now checked in the SELECT list too. Three parser traps found and closed by running it repo-wide, each of which would have made the guard cry wolf: `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM x)` truncating the list at a depth-1 `FROM`; `trim(both ' ' FROM col)` position keywords sitting in column position; and quoted camelCase output aliases (`AS "vendorName"`) surviving the upstream lowercase. Line 4 fires BEFORE either.** **CC-3's LIVE EVIDENCE that this is the real-world path, not a theoretical one:** across this session the drop failed **four separate times** — CC-3 pointer-drag ×1, CC-3 keyboard-drag ×2 (the dnd-kit keyboard sensor moved the overlay by pixel steps and never snapped to a droppable), and **once by a human**, who then reported the load as moved to *Completed*. **Every one produced: no HTTP request, NO `audit.row_changes` row, `updated_at` unmoved, and NO toast of any kind.** For `L-20260806-0008` the audit trail ended at the Gate-A hop `07:14:33.413711` with nothing after it — proving the mutation was never called. **A refused transition would have produced a request, a throw, a revert and an error toast; none appeared.** **WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS:** this is the failure mode that made a human report a status change that never happened — the same class the board has spent four PRs closing, and the only one still open. **A dispatcher cannot distinguish 'the server refused' from 'my drag missed the lane' from 'it worked'.** On a board with 11 lanes, a near-miss release is the ordinary case, not the edge case. **PERMANENT FIX — DEFINITION OF DONE:** (1) **root cause** — when a drag ends with no resolved droppable, do not return bare: restore/keep state and surface a neutral hint (*"Drop the card onto a lane to change its status"*). **It is NOT an error** — the user simply missed — so it must not read as a failure; **but it must not be silence.** (2) **Also consider line 16**, `if (resolveKanbanColumnKey(load) === targetColumnKey) return;` — silent by design (dropping a card into the lane it already occupies is a true no-op), so **lower priority**; a brief *"already in <lane>"* would still beat nothing. **CC-3 is not calling that one a defect.** (3) **a WIRED guard** extending `verify-kanban-dropstatus-contract.mjs` (step **2815**): assert **every** early-return branch in `handleDragEnd` either mutates state or calls `pushToast` — the class fix, so branch #5 cannot be added silently later. (4) **live proof** — a release outside any lane produces visible feedback and leaves the card where it was. **CC-3 changed no FE code.** | (cc-2/kanban-drop-outside-droppable) | **DONE — PR #4826.** All three early returns in `handleDragEnd` now speak: the outside-droppable release shows the neutral `info` hint CC-3 specified, the same-lane drop says "already in <lane>", and the synthetic truck card (unreachable since #4793) is left feedback-bearing so the class rule has no exception. Guard = the CLASS rule requested, `auditDragEndBranchesSpeak()` in the already-wired step 2815: ANY early return in this handler that neither toasts nor changes state fails CI, so branch #6 cannot be added silently. Mutation-proven against the real file (restore the bare return → exit 1; restored → exit 0, byte-identical); selftest 25 mutations. **CC-3's evidence reversed a judgment CC-2 had made hours earlier in #4824** — CC-2 had treated the outside-droppable release as an expected no-op and kept it silent; the measured human report of a load "moved" that never moved beats that reasoning. ## OPEN · CC-1 · P1 · SETTLEMENT-LOAD-COUNT-IGNORES-DIRECT-LINK — "Loads" reads 0 on every settlement that has one
**Found by CC-3, UI prove of ACCT-F271 on prod `d236753`, then traced to source and confirmed on Neon.**

**UI:** `/driver-finance/settlements` shows `Loads = 0` for **all 7** settlements, including two that demonstrably
cover a load: `S-20260808-0085` (Jorge Pablo Guadalupe Muñoz Gonzalez, $935.10) and `S-20260808-0090`
(Rafael Rogelio Rivero Reynoso, $410.00).

**ROOT CAUSE — two different load linkages, and the list reads only one.**
`settlements.routes.ts:145-152` computes:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT db.load_id) FROM driver_finance.settlement_lines sl
JOIN driver_finance.driver_bills db ON db.id = sl.source_driver_bill_id
WHERE sl.settlement_id = s.id AND db.load_id IS NOT NULL
```
It reaches the load **only through `source_driver_bill_id → driver_bills.load_id`** and **ignores
`settlement_lines.load_id` entirely.** Measured on prod for both settlements above:
```
lines = 1 · lines_direct_load_id = 1 · lines_with_src_bill = 0 · bills_with_load = 0
```
So the line **does** carry a direct `load_id`, has **no** source driver bill, and the count is structurally 0.
`SettlementsTable.tsx:54-59` renders `Number(row.load_count ?? 0)`, so the miss displays as a confident `0`.

**WHY IT MATTERS / RELATION TO ACCT-F271:** #5017 fills the bookends from the settlement's own lines. **The list
column does not read the bookends and does not read `settlement_lines.load_id`** — so #5017 can work perfectly
and this column will still show `0`. Two linkages that must agree currently disagree, and the surface a user
actually looks at reports the wrong one. Under the connectivity law a settlement must be able to say which loads
it covers; today it says "none".

**ASK:** make `load_count` count the union — `COALESCE(sl.load_id, db.load_id)` — or state which linkage is
canonical and backfill the other. **Do not "fix" it by inventing `source_driver_bill_id` values.**
**CC-3 verifies after deploy; CC-3 does not build it.**

## ROOT CAUSE (CC-3, prod `1be9c64`) for DELIVERED-LOAD-NO-DRIVER-PAY — **driver pay is CREATE-TIME-ONLY, and only from one creator**
**Traced in source, verified against the whole write-path population. This makes the P0 actionable.**

**1. There are exactly TWO writers of `driver_finance.driver_bills` in the entire backend, and they are the same
file:** `dispatch/book-load.service.ts:543` and `:612`. Nothing else inserts a driver bill —
`grep "INSERT INTO driver_finance.driver_bills"` across `apps/backend/src` (tests excluded) returns those two.

**2. No lifecycle transition mints pay.** `dispatch/update-load.service.ts` touches `driver_bills` at **`:238`
only to READ it for the edit lock** (`driver_bill_locked`). Assign, dispatch, in-transit, delivered,
`delivered_pending_docs` and `completed_docs_received` mint nothing.

**3. The other load creator never mints.** `mdata/loads.routes.ts` creates loads **with** a driver and neither
mints pay nor audits a skip — this is already the standing OPEN P1 `KNOWN GAP` in
`scripts/verify-load-creators-mint-or-audit-driver-pay.mjs` (guard currently `ok`, gap still listed).

**⇒ CONCLUSION: driver pay exists only if the load was booked through `book-load.service.ts`. A load created by
any other path is PERMANENTLY unpaid — there is no later transition that can rescue it, because delivery does not
mint.** That fully explains $13,186.50 of delivered freight with no pay artifact, and it explains why a pay rate
on file predicts nothing.

**This also raises the stakes on three guards that all name the same file** — `verify-load-creators-mint-or-audit-driver-pay`
(pay), `verify-load-write-paths-run-driver-qualification` (#4988, qualification),
`verify-driver-reassign-runs-qualification` (#5009, reassign). **`mdata/loads.routes.ts` is a driver-seating
write path that skips pay, qualification AND reassign checks.** It is one file behind three separate P1s.

**ASK:** either route `mdata/loads.routes.ts` through the same mint as `book-load.service.ts`, or add a mint at
the delivery transition so pay cannot depend on which creator was used. **Prefer the delivery transition** — pay
is earned on delivery, and a create-time-only mint can never recover a load booked by any future creator.

| **OPEN (P1 · verification-integrity · ALL LANES)** `CLS-FALSE-ZERO-INSTRUMENTS` — **three different instruments each handed me a confident, well-formed ZERO in one session; every one of them would have become a filed defect or a false green if I had trusted it** | needs one: any zero-based assertion must carry a same-statement/same-run positive control | C | **ALL SEATS (method law — CC-2 filed)** | **Not theory — three live instances in one CC-2 session, each caught only because a control was demanded.** **(1) NEON MCP ROLE ROUTING.** The tool lands on `ih35_app` on some calls and `neondb_owner` on others, same tool, same branch, minutes apart. As `ih35_app` the `app.bypass_rls` GUC reads back `'on'` and does **NOTHING** — RLS still filters to zero because no `app.current_user_id` / `app.operating_company_id` is set. `SELECT current_user, current_setting('app.bypass_rls',true), count(*)` returned **`ih35_app` / `on` / `0`** in one row while a neighbouring transaction counted **12,014** invoices on the same table. I was one step from filing "views.ar_aging returns 0 rows while 297 open invoices exist" as an A/R linkage defect; it does not survive a same-statement control. **RULE: `current_user` and a must-be-non-zero control belong in the SAME STATEMENT as any count on an RLS table — a control in a neighbouring statement of the same transaction is NOT sufficient**, and `bypass_seen='on'` is not evidence bypass applied. **(2) EXIT CODE THROUGH A PIPE.** `git push … | tail -6` run in the background reported **exit 0** while the push had actually FAILED (`husky - pre-push script failed`); the pipe returns tail's status. I reported "push completed" on that basis and was wrong. **Never pipe a hooked git command whose exit code you intend to read.** **(3) PREMATURE COMPLETION DETECTION.** An `until grep -q "verify-static" <logfile>` wait-loop matched npm's own `> node scripts/verify-static.mjs` echo line on the first poll and exited immediately, yielding "0 failures" for a run that had not started. A second baseline attempt used a fresh `git worktree` with **no `node_modules`**, so `npm run verify:static` died instantly and reported "1 failure" — a number that means nothing. **Both were discarded rather than reported; a worktree baseline needs `node_modules` symlinked or the comparison is void.** **WHY THIS IS A BOARD ROW AND NOT A NOTE:** the existing law already says an empty result is an instrument claim, and I still nearly filed one — because each of these zeros arrived *well-formed*, from a tool that had just worked. The discriminator has to be mechanical (a control column that MUST come back non-zero), not a reminder to be careful. | — | **FIXED · OWNER-GATED=no** |

The call sites since moved to `entityLabel(name, id, noun)` and `selectedCompanyId ?? ""`, so the guards reddened **because of the improvement**. **LIVE PROOF THE SCREENS WERE NEVER BROKEN** (browser, CC-2 seat, prod): `/safety/accidents` renders `Juan USMCA-Battery · TEST-UNIT-20260806-01 · L-20260806-0005`; `/safety/internal-fines` renders 5 rows, every driver fully named. Zero uuids on either. **THIS IS WHY THE FIX IS NOT A PAGE PATCH** — editing AccidentsPage to restore the inline spelling would have deleted a real control (see below) to satisfy a blind regex. **WHY WIDENING DOES NOT WEAKEN:** `entityLabel` is a SUPERSET of the inline form and is itself guarded (`verify-entity-label-rejects-uuid-shaped-name`, live 0 / selftest 0) — it additionally rejects a **uuid-shaped value arriving in the NAME column**, which the inline `\|\| "Unit"` spelling renders verbatim. It now slices to the `label={…}` attribute that references the field. **★ THE SUBTLEST MEMBER:** `verify-drivers-team-create-picker` had a **PASSING selftest and a failing live run** — its fixture still used the bare literal, so it was green against a fiction and red against the real file. A selftest that never reads the real file cannot tell you the detector still works. Its fixture now carries both spellings, plus the negative cases it never had (picker with NO scope prop → caught on both fields; picker scoped to a hardcoded uuid → caught). **MUTATION-PROVEN ON THE REAL PAGES, exit codes read without a pipe:** AccidentsPage driver label → `label={row.driver_id}` ⇒ accidents-list rc=1 AND damage-honesty rc=1, restored rc=0; PositionHistoryPage → `label={row.unit_number ?? row.unit_id}` ⇒ rc=1, restored rc=0; Drivers.tsx scope prop deleted ⇒ rc=1, restored rc=0. `verify-safety-accident-damage-label-honesty` previously had **no label mutation at all** — its selftest only exercised the damage-photo branch, certifying an assertion it never touched; it now carries 3 label mutations + a legacy-spelling acceptance case. **NOT CLAIMED:** static analysis of JSX attributes. It proves each call site asks for a resolved label; it does not prove the API supplied a name for any given row. | sha pending (this PR) | **VERIFIED (CASCADE WAVE-TONIGHT 2026-08-16; was FIXED)** |

| **FIXED (P1 · dead picker · CC-2 lane)** `F-17 / LV-CLASS-PICKER-OVER-CAP` — **the Manual JE and Driver Detail class pickers were not slow or capped, they were 400ing on open; and the guard that narrates this exact failure mode never asserted it** | `scripts/verify-no-silent-list-caps.mjs` (registered step 2646) — over-cap check added as a HARD ZERO; mutation-proven | C | **CC-2 (mine — fixed in this PR)** | **ROOT CAUSE, both sides read, not guessed.** `apps/frontend/src/api/accounting.ts:1378` requested `/api/v1/catalogs/classes?include_inactive=false&limit=300` while `apps/backend/src/catalogs/classes.routes.ts:12` declares `limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(200)`. The request 400s, so the picker renders empty — not a capped list, a DEAD one, with no rows and no error surfaced. **LIVE ON PROD (browser, CC-2 seat, USMCA):** the same endpoint answers **400 at limit=300** and **200 at limit=200, returning 2 classes**. **ONE FIX, THREE QUEUE ITEMS:** `listClassesForJe` is the only class fetch in the frontend and is consumed by `ManualJEModal.tsx:55` AND `DriverDetail.tsx:293`, so F-17, F-20 and F-09 are the same site. **CHECKED AND NOT FILED:** `FleetTablePage.tsx:77` sends `limit=500` to `/api/v1/mdata/units`, whose schema declares `max(500)` — legal, so it is NOT a defect and I did not file it. **★ THE GUARD DESCRIBED THIS DEFECT IN PROSE AND ASSERTED NOTHING ABOUT IT.** `verify-no-silent-list-caps.mjs`'s own header says of the drivers instance: *"the cap exceeded the backend's own max, so the request 400'd and the export produced no file AND no error"* — yet the guard only ever compared FE page sizes against a silent-cap baseline, which had nothing to say here because the request never returned a list at all. Documentation is not enforcement. It now resolves each FE `limit=N` against the `z…max(M)` declared in the route file that owns that path and fails when N > M — a HARD ZERO, not a ratchet, because exceeding a declared max is a guaranteed 400 and never a judgement call. | **INVESTIGATED — confirmed NOT a defect, do not "fix" (CC-1, 2026-08-12 ~10:00 CT)** `LV-JE-STATUS-VOIDED-SPELLING-GAP-CLOSED-NOT-A-BUG` — closes the follow-up flagged in `ACCT-F368` (~13 `je.status <> 'voided'` sites) | `apps/backend/src/accounting/{balance-sheet,cash-flow,trial-balance,profit-loss,account-register,month-close,finance-hub}.service.ts` (read-only investigation, no code changed) | C | CC-1 (money/GL) | Continuing the same-cycle sweep, this time to a definitive CLOSE rather than another open question. `journal-entries.service.ts`'s own documentation confirms: **a voided JE's original row is NEVER flipped to `status='voided'`** — it stays `posted`; only a NEW, separate reversing JE is created (equal and opposite legs). So every `je.status <> 'voided'` clause in these ~13 sites is a literal that matches ZERO rows, always — but this is **NOT a defect**, for two independently-confirmed reasons: **(1) Aggregate reports** (trial-balance, balance-sheet, cash-flow, profit-loss, month-close, finance-hub) `SUM()`/`GROUP BY` postings across accounts — a voided JE's original posting AND its reversal's posting are BOTH included, and by construction they are equal-and-opposite, so they **net to zero**. The dead clause changes nothing because correctness here comes from double-entry math, not from excluding rows. ## OPEN · CC-1 · P1 · LV-JE-MEMO-RECORD-NOT-VISIBLE — Manual Journal Entries list shows "Record — not visible" for ~130 of 146 real, live, resolvable rows
**Found live 2026-08-16 during accounting Wave A3 live-verify of the `je.list` leaf** (`/accounting/journal-entries`, selected-USMCA). 130+ of 146 posted JE memos read like `"Expense Record — not visible posting"`, `"Bill payment Record — not visible posting"`, `"Reversal of Record — not visible"`, `"Bank categorization Record — not visible posting"` — the placeholder noun `"Record — not visible"` appears in place of what should be the real source record's identity, even though every one of these source records IS live, real, and independently viewable elsewhere in the app (already directly confirmed this session for expenses, bill payments, bills — see ACCT-F5394/5395/5396/5397 fixes).

**ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by code read, not fixed today — scope larger than a single-function patch):**
`humanMemo()` in `apps/frontend/src/pages/accounting/ManualJEListPage.tsx:26-29` does:
```ts
const UUID_RE = /[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}/gi;
function humanMemo(memo) {
  if (!memo) return "—";
  return memo.replace(UUID_RE, (uuid) => entityLabel(null, uuid, "Record"));
}
```
It regex-matches every UUID embedded in the free-text memo and replaces it with `entityLabel(null, uuid, "Record")` — the `name` argument is **hardcoded `null`**, so `entityLabel` can *never* resolve anything and always falls back to its `"<noun> — not visible"` string, regardless of whether the UUID is genuinely resolvable. This is not a data problem — it's a display function that structurally cannot succeed. Per the `LST-F107` comment two lines below it, this replacement exists to satisfy "JE column must not lead with a bare UUID fragment" — so simply reverting to show the raw UUID would regress that earlier fix.

**Same shape, other pages** (found while tracing this): `PostingLineagePage.tsx`'s `PostingEntityLink` and `QboReconcileCapturesPage.tsx`, `AccountingAuditTrailPage.tsx` all default their label to `entityLabel(null, id, "Record")` too when no name is separately threaded in — the systemic gap is "we never built a generic `source_transaction_type + source_transaction_id → display name` resolver," not a per-page typo.

**Why not fixed inline today:** `JournalEntry` rows already carry `source_transaction_type` / `source_transaction_id` as first-class columns (`apps/frontend/src/api/accounting.ts:1360-1361`) — a real fix should resolve a name via those typed fields (mirroring `postingEntityKind()` in `PostingLineagePage.tsx`) and render a real `<EntityLink>`, not keep parsing memo text. That requires either (a) a new generic backend resolver endpoint, or (b) per-source-type name lookups already available from sibling list endpoints — a genuine design decision spanning ≥4 pages, not a same-turn scoped fix, and risks regressing `LST-F107` if rushed.

**Live evidence:** `/accounting/journal-entries`, selected USMCA, 146 rows, backend `d86f234c9`+ (session tip), LIVE 2026-08-16. No mutation performed.

**Ask:** whoever picks this up — build the typed `source_transaction_type`/`source_transaction_id` → real `<EntityLink>` resolution path (reusing `postingEntityKind()`'s kind-mapping) for `ManualJEListPage.humanMemo`/`journalEntryListLabel`, and audit the other 3 sibling `entityLabel(null, id, "Record")` call sites for the same fix. Add a guard proving JE memo rendering resolves a real name/link for every row whose `source_transaction_type` is known, not just presence of a UUID substring.

## OPEN · CC-1 · P2 · LV-INVOICES-LIST-SHOWS-30-OF-37 — Invoices list undercounts USMCA rows vs the transactions register
**Found live 2026-08-16 during accounting Wave A3 live-verify** (cross-checking `je.list`/`transactions` leaves against the earlier `invoices.list` leaf). `/accounting/invoices` (selected USMCA, no filters applied — default state) shows **"1–30 of 30"**. `/accounting/transactions` (the "All Transactions" register, same company, same underlying invoices) surfaces at least 3 invoice numbers NOT present anywhere on the Invoices list page in the same session (`INV-2026-00030`, `INV-2026-00033`, `INV-2026-00034`, all `void`).

**Live-confirmed via direct SQL (bypass-RLS, single combined query — ACCT-F5391-safe):** `accounting.invoices` for USMCA operating_company_id `5c854333-6ea5-4faa-af31-67cb272fef80` has **37** total rows, and the EXACT query behind `GET /api/v1/accounting/invoices`'s COUNT (`apps/backend/src/accounting/invoices.routes.ts` — `INNER JOIN mdata.customers` on `customer_id` + `operating_company_id`, no extra filters) returns **37** when run with the same bypass. Every one of the 37 invoices' `customer_id` resolves to a real `mdata.customers` row (confirmed via `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE c.id IS NULL` returning 0 rows) — so it is **not** a broken/missing customer FK causing an INNER JOIN drop.

**Not yet root-caused:** the live app (real Owner session, not bypass) only returns 30. Since the SQL is provably correct under bypass, the gap is either (a) `mdata.customers` RLS behaving more restrictively for this session than CLAUDE.md law #4's "Owner sessions see all entities via `org.user_accessible_company_ids()`" would predict, or (b) some other server-side filter/limit not visible from the route source I read. This needs the query re-run through the REAL authenticated session path (not a bypass script) to see which 7 invoices/customers get filtered and why — I could not do that live-verify safely without either mutating auth state or guessing, so I'm boarding it rather than shipping an RLS-adjacent fix on a guess.

**Live evidence:** `/accounting/invoices` "1–30 of 30"; `/accounting/transactions` page 1 showing `INV-2026-00030`/`00033`/`00034`; USMCA `5c854333-6ea5-4faa-af31-67cb272fef80`; backend session tip `d86f234c9`+; LIVE 2026-08-16. No mutation performed.

**Ask:** whoever picks this up — reproduce via the real authenticated route (add temporary logging or a `--as-user` debug flag to `listAllBillsForCompany`'s invoice sibling, or diff the RLS policy on `mdata.customers`/`accounting.invoices` against what Owner should see), identify the 7 missing invoices, and confirm whether they belong to customers that are somehow scoped differently (e.g. `deactivated_at` on the customer, a stricter policy predicate than company-id). Do not "fix" by loosening RLS without understanding why it's filtering first.

Full guard files, embedded here since the branch that authored them was never pushed (local-only commit, not retrievable by another session) — `scripts/verify-invoice-create-modal-customer-entitylink.mjs`:
```js
import fs from "node:fs";

const file = "apps/frontend/src/pages/accounting/InvoiceCreateModal.tsx";
const source = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");

function failures(text) {
  const errors = [];
  const columnMatch = text.match(/key:\s*"customer",\s*label:\s*"Customer"[\s\S]{0,800}?key:\s*"status"/);
  if (!columnMatch) {
    errors.push("could not locate the Customer column definition (file restructured?)");
    return errors;
  }
  const block = columnMatch[0];
  if (!/load\.customer_id\s*\?/.test(block)) errors.push("Customer column does not branch on load.customer_id");
  if (!/kind="customer"/.test(block)) errors.push("Customer column does not render an EntityLink kind=\"customer\"");
  if (!/id=\{load\.customer_id\}/.test(block)) errors.push("Customer column's EntityLink is not wired to load.customer_id");
  return errors;
}

if (process.argv.includes("--selftest")) {
  const regressed = source.replace(
    /render:\s*\(load\)\s*=>\s*\n\s*load\.customer_id\s*\?\s*\(\s*\n\s*<EntityLink kind="customer"[\s\S]{0,220}?\)\s*:\s*\(\s*\n\s*entityLabel\(load\.customer_name, load\.customer_id, "Customer"\)\s*\n\s*\),/,
    'render: (load) => entityLabel(load.customer_name, load.customer_id, "Customer"),',
  );
  const ok = failures(source).length === 0;
  const catchesRegression = failures(regressed).includes("Customer column does not branch on load.customer_id");
  if (!ok || !catchesRegression) {
    console.error("verify-invoice-create-modal-customer-entitylink selftest FAIL", { ok, catchesRegression });
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log("verify-invoice-create-modal-customer-entitylink selftest PASS — reverting to bare entityLabel turns red");
  process.exit(0);
}

const errors = failures(source);
if (errors.length) {
  console.error(`verify-invoice-create-modal-customer-entitylink FAIL:\n- ${errors.join("\n- ")}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(
  "verify-invoice-create-modal-customer-entitylink PASS — the from-load invoice pick table's Customer column drills through a real EntityLink, matching the Load # column's C5 fix",
);
```

| **CRITICAL-OPEN (CC-2 2026-08-24, /system leftover sweep):** `INFRA-F6350-PROD-WORKERS-SILENT-STOP-SINCE-0821` — `/system` (Owner-only) shows `Software / Build: DEGRADED`, `Object store · Email · Jobs: RED`, `background_jobs.stale: DOWN`. Direct Neon confirms this is real and severe, not a UI artifact: **`outbox.events` has 156 rows pending delivery, zero of them with any `retry_count` or `last_error` (i.e. never even attempted), oldest from 2026-08-21, last successful delivery 2026-08-21T22:03 UTC** — includes `expense.created.unattributed` (128), `tms.{vendor,invoice,customer,bill}.push_requested`, `fmcsa.customer.verify_requested`, `driver_finance.settlement.{opened,payment_due,closed}`. **`_system.background_jobs` shows ~85 distinct cron jobs (QBO sync, Samsara telemetry, fraud detector, email queue, insurance/compliance reminders, driver settlement auto-pay, audit chain verify, etc.) all frozen at `last_successful_run_at` timestamps clustered 2026-06-08 through 2026-08-21T22:39 UTC** — while a *separate* set of 5-6 jobs registered via a different code path (`scheduler/jobs.index.ts` → `registerComplianceSchedulerJobs`, called from `compliance.routes.ts`, NOT behind the same gate) run fine as recently as minutes ago. This is still live on the CURRENT deploy (`189dd4c`, re-curled). Root cause (Explore-agent read of `apps/backend/src/index.ts` + `apps/backend/src/outbox/{processor,index}.ts` + git history, code-only, no infra access): `apps/backend/src/index.ts:1746` gates `startOutboxProcessor()` behind `!bootApiSmoke && process.env.ENABLE_OUTBOX_PROCESSOR !== "false"`, and `index.ts:1210` gates ~20 `initialize*Cron()` calls behind the same `!bootApiSmoke` (`process.env.IH35_BOOT_API_SMOKE === "true"`, `index.ts:1183`). | TASK-F6360-ID-SCOPE-ALWAYS-404 | FIXED (THIS PR) | CC-2 tasks leftover unique silent no-op | `apps/backend/src/tasks/task.routes.ts`; `apps/frontend/src/api/tasks.ts`; `apps/frontend/src/pages/tasks/TasksChatPage.tsx`; `scripts/verify-tasks-id-scope-rls-fix.mjs` (verify-step 4655) | While sweeping `/tasks` leftover unique, Team Chat's `/tasks/chat?taskId=...` consistently rendered honest-looking "No comments yet. Start the conversation." / "No activity yet." for a real task with real activity elsewhere in the app — live network capture (correct absolute API origin, not the frontend's SPA fallback which produced a false 200 on a first mistaken pass) showed `GET .../comments` and `GET .../activity` both returning **404 `{"error":"Task not found"}`**, every load, for a task visibly listed on the Task Board. Root cause: all seven `:id`-scoped task routes (`PATCH /:id/status`, `GET /:id`, `GET/POST /:id/links`, `PATCH /:id/progress`, `GET/POST /:id/comments`, `GET /:id/activity`) tried to bootstrap RLS scope by reading `tasks.task` UNSCOPED first (`SELECT operating_company_id FROM tasks.task WHERE task_id = $1`) before calling `SET_TASK_SCOPE_SQL` — but `tasks.task` is FORCE RLS on `app.current_operating_company_id` (confirmed live via `pg_policy`), and `withCurrentUser()` never sets that GUC, so the bootstrap read is itself blocked and always returns zero rows. Every one of these seven routes has 404'd "Task not found" for every real task, for every user, always — the frontend's honest-looking empty states masked a completely broken backend, not an actual empty comment/activity list. Fix: added `operating_company_id` as a required query param (the same trusted-input pattern every OTHER route in this file already uses — `ListTasksQuerySchema`, `PlannerQuerySchema`, `CreateTaskBodySchema`), set RLS scope from it FIRST, then query once — a caller passing the wrong company still gets a correct 404 via RLS, not cross-tenant access, so no security regression. Updated the 3 frontend callers actually wired into the UI (`fetchTaskComments`/`createTaskComment`/`fetchTaskActivity` in `TasksChatPage.tsx`, alongside Codex's concurrent `TASK-F6336-CHAT-COMMENT-FAILS-SILENTLY` frontend error-surfacing fix on the same file — both landed cleanly, no conflict) plus the 3 currently-unwired ones (`updateTaskProgress`, `fetchTaskLinks`, `createTaskLink`) at the root so they don't repeat this bug when a future PR wires them up. New guard: 18 independently mutation-proven cases (backend route-by-route + frontend function-by-function + page call-site-by-call-site). Same bug class also latent on the sibling expense branch (`autoCreateExpenseFromWO`/`paid_same_day`) since it shares the identical copy function, just never hit the CHECK because `expense_lines` has no equivalent constraint — the $0 row would have silently reached the poster there too. | `apps/backend/src/maintenance/two-section-service.ts` (`copyToAccountingLines`); `scripts/verify-wo-bill-zero-line-je-check.mjs` | A | **CC-3 — same file/session as #15933, contained data-copy fix, no new GL math** | Exclude `total_cost = 0` rows from the `work_order_lines` source query `copyToAccountingLines` already shares between the bill and expense branches — a $0 line is never a real financial line item (already excluded from Section B's own total via the existing `max(own, sub_total)` computation) and contributes nothing to either branch's posting math. Sub_rows still copy with their real amounts; their `parent_line_uuid` mapping simply resolves to null when their own $0 container was excluded (structural nesting loses one level for zero-value parents, not a regression since that parent was never a real cost line). The "Income Accuracy" / "Net Variance" cards derived from this comparison are therefore not measuring prediction accuracy at all — they mechanically show ~0% projected / ~100%+ variance for any day where a load actually completed its full lifecycle, silently manufacturing a plausible-looking but meaningless number (matches the `silent-failures-manufacture-a-plausible-normal-value` class: no error, no 500, just a wrong-by-construction figure that looks like real accuracy data). | `apps/backend/src/cash-flow/cash-flow.service.ts:611-715` (`getActualVsProjected()`'s `projIncomeSql` — needs a persisted daily snapshot of what was projected as-of that day, e.g. a `cash_flow_projection_snapshots` table written once per day by a cron/job, so historical rows compare against a frozen prediction instead of a live re-query); consumed by `apps/backend/src/cash-flow/cash-flow.routes.ts:71-89` and `apps/frontend` cash-flow "Actual vs Projected" tab | B | **CC-1 — money/finance lane (this changes what a financial accuracy metric actually measures; a new snapshot table + write path is migration-shaped, not a same-turn FE fix)** | Add a daily snapshot job that persists `getDailyPrediction()`'s output once per day (e.g. at midnight or via the existing outbox/cron pattern) into a new append-only table keyed by `(operating_company_id, prediction_date, captured_at)`; point `getActualVsProjected()` at that snapshot for any `date < today` instead of the live query, keeping the live query only for `date >= today` (today's own not-yet-final prediction). Add a regression guard asserting a snapshot row exists and is used for any historical date in range. NOT attempting this fix myself — it is a migration + new write path, squarely CC-1's lane, not a live-verify same-turn scope. | Live `/cash-flow` "Actual vs Projected" tab on healthz `f12ab6e`, USMCA, fresh page load: screenshot shows Income Accuracy Proj \$0.00 / Act \$5,300.00 and all 4 visible rows with Projected Income \$0.00 against real nonzero Actual Income; root cause read directly from `cash-flow.service.ts`'s `getActualVsProjected()` showing no snapshot table and a live re-query gated on load/invoice state that only **FIXED CODE · CC-1 2026-08-26:** built the daily-snapshot fix exactly as this row specified. New table forecast.cash_flow_projection_snapshots (append-only: FORCE RLS + lucia-bypass policy, GRANT SELECT/INSERT then explicit REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE since forecast's own schema-level ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES would otherwise silently widen it; rehearsed on a disposable Neon branch, applied+verified on PROD). New daily cron (cash-flow-projection-snapshot.cron.ts, 06:10 America/Chicago) captures each active company's getDailyPrediction().income_subtotal_cents for 'today' before that day's loads can complete their lifecycle; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keeps every snapshot frozen once captured. getActualVsProjected() now reads the snapshot for any date strictly before today (company business date) and overrides the live-recomputed value; today itself stays live per this row's own guidance; a date with no snapshot row falls back to the pre-existing live query, never worse than before. USING (true)` policy (`equipment_types_select_all` in `db/migrations/0017_equipment_types_catalog.sql:48-50`; `dls_select_all` in `db/migrations/0019_cust_driver_fields.sql:97-99` — the 0017 migration's own comment even says "Shared global catalog... Used by units, equipment (trailers)..."). Both were LATER converted to per-entity tables (`db/migrations/202607910000_equipment_types_per_entity.sql`; `db/migrations/202607870000_driver_load_statuses_per_entity.sql`) — each migration adds `operating_company_id` (verified on prod: 100% non-null, zero shared/NULL rows — genuinely entity-partitioned data, not shared-canonical), backfills+seeds real per-company rows for every entity, and adds a correctly-scoped `company_scope` policy (`identity.is_lucia_bypass() OR operating_company_id::text = current_setting('app.operating_company_id', true)`). **But neither per-entity-conversion migration ever DROPs the original `_select_all`/`dls_select_all` policy.** Since Postgres RLS permissive policies for the same command are logically OR'd, a row is visible under SELECT if it satisfies EITHER policy — so the leftover unconditional-`true` policy silently continues to grant full cross-entity read access to EVERY row, completely defeating the newer `company_scope` policy for all SELECTs, regardless of which `app.operating_company_id` GUC is set. Confirmed live on prod (`br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a`): `pg_policy` for `catalogs.equipment_types` shows BOTH `company_scope` (`polcmd='*'`, scoped) AND `equipment_types_select_all` (`polcmd='r'`, `USING (true)`) simultaneously active; `catalogs.equipment_types` itself has real per-company data (USMCA 11 rows, TRANSP 7, TRK 7, zero NULL-opco). Grep confirmed `driver_load_statuses` has the identical `dls_select_all` `USING(true)` leftover. **Downstream consumer already read this hop:** `apps/backend/src/catalogs/catalog-registry.routes.ts`'s `fetchCatalogStats()`/`fetchPreviewItems()` (feeding `/lists`'s Catalog Registry stats+preview for the `EQUIPMENT_TYPES` and `DRIVER_LOAD_STATUSES` registry entries) issue their SQL with NO explicit `WHERE operating_company_id = $1` clause at all for these two catalogs specifically (unlike `CHART_OF_ACCOUNTS`/`CLASSES`, which DO carry an explicit `AND operating_company_id = $1::uuid` in their preview SQL as defense-in-depth) — meaning this consumer was RELYING ENTIRELY on RLS to scope these two catalogs, and RLS is not actually doing that job for them. Live impact: any operator viewing the Equipment Types or Driver Load Statuses registry entry sees stats/preview counts aggregated across ALL THREE entities (USMCA+TRANSP+TRK combined), not just their own — a real, live, currently-active cross-entity data leak, not merely a masked-by-RLS false-empty. | **OPEN (CC-3 2026-08-28, found while chasing `BOOK-LOAD-MODAL-INVISIBLE-BEHIND-DRAWER` on `/dispatch`, NOT built — precise root cause read from source, not guessed, but the real fix is its own PR):** `DISPATCH-SEARCH-BOX-KEYSTROKE-LOSS` — the "Load #, customer, stop city…" filter box on `/dispatch?view=list` / `?view=kanban` (`apps/frontend/src/components/dispatch/FilterBar.tsx:126-133`, `TableSearch` component) only ever retains the LAST character typed: type "0857" and the URL's `search=` param ends up `search=7`. Confirmed live 2026-08-28: typing into the box character-by-character loses everything but the final keystroke; navigating directly to `?search=L-20260827-0857` (bypassing the input) filters correctly (`Showing 1-1 of 1 load`) — so the search/filter LOGIC itself is fine, this is purely a lost-keystroke input bug. **ROOT CAUSE, read from source, not inferred:** `TableSearch.tsx` binds a fully-controlled `<input value={value} onChange={...} onInput={...}>` to `value.search`, where `value` (`FilterBar`'s `value` prop) is sourced all the way from `Dispatch.tsx`'s `filters = useMemo(() => parseFilters(searchParams, ...), [searchParams])` — i.e. the box's displayed value round-trips through `setSearchParams` → React Router navigation → route re-render → `useMemo` recompute → prop flow back down, on EVERY keystroke (`FilterBar.tsx:129`: `onChange={(search) => onChange({ ...value, search })}`, wired at `Dispatch.tsx:244` straight into `setSearchParams`). `TableSearch.tsx` ALSO attaches native (non-React) `input`/`change` listeners in a `useEffect` (added for `LV-FLEET-SEARCH-NO-FILTER`, Live/CDP automation compatibility) with `[onChange, value]` in the dependency array — since `FilterBar`'s `onChange` prop is a fresh inline arrow function every render (`FilterBar.tsx:129`), this effect tears down and re-attaches its native listeners on every keystroke's resulting re-render, racing against the controlled `value` prop's own slow URL round-trip. Net effect: a fully-controlled input driven by async, per-keystroke browser-navigation-based state, with no local buffering — a classic controlled-input-lag pattern that manifests exactly as "typed text doesn't stick." | `apps/frontend/src/components/dispatch/FilterBar.tsx:126-133`; `apps/frontend/src/pages/Dispatch.tsx:104,163,169,244` (`useSearchParams`, `filters` useMemo, the `setSearchParams` onChange wiring); `apps/frontend/src/components/table/TableSearch.tsx` (the shared component itself — also used elsewhere, so this may not be dispatch-only; not checked on other pages this hop) | B | **CC-3 — mechanical FE lane (dispatch chrome)** | Give `TableSearch` (or just this call site) a local `useState` buffer for the visible input value, syncing FROM the `value` prop only when it's genuinely external (e.g. a Reset click), and debouncing the outward `onChange`→`setSearchParams` call (e.g. 250-400ms) instead of firing on every keystroke synchronously into a URL-navigation round trip. Also worth checking whether the `[onChange, value]` effect-teardown-per-render on the native-listener `useEffect` is itself contributing (stabilize `FilterBar`'s `onChange` prop with `useCallback` regardless). Verify against the `LV-FLEET-SEARCH-NO-FILTER` fixture this component was built for — the fix must keep native-value-set (CDP/automation) detection working, not just the human-typing path. A genuinely new mechanism, not a repeat of GO-0032 (export dead-click) or GO-0037 (date-range order on the accounting cash-flow statement route — a separate surface from this one). `ManualDailyProjectionsTab.tsx`'s "Pull bills / expenses / payments" action (`pullMutation`) POSTs one `createForecastEntry()` per candidate row, sequentially, deduping against an in-memory `existingKeys` set rebuilt each run from the React Query cache (`allEntries`). `POST /api/v1/forecast/cash-entries` is rate-limited to 30/min; a real backlog pull (up to ~400 candidate rows across bills/expenses/payments/invoices, each capped at `limit: 100`) can exceed that mid-loop, throwing AFTER some rows already committed to `forecast.cash_entries` (which has no unique constraint beyond its own auto-generated `id` — `db/migrations/202606161800_cash_forecast_manual.sql:20`). `onSuccess` invalidated the entries query cache; `onError` did NOT — so a user who saw the generic "Pull from software failed" message and clicked the SAME button again (the natural retry, not disabled after a failure — only while `pullMutation.isPending`) rebuilt `existingKeys` from the STALE cache, missing the rows that already landed, and re-created them. If the retry then succeeds in full, `onSuccess` fires and clears `pullError` entirely — the UI ends in a clean, error-free state with Expected Expenses/Income and Projected Closing silently double-counting the duplicated rows; the only trace is two rows sharing the same invoice/bill number, easy to miss among dozens of pulled lines. | **RESOLVED — NOT A DEFECT (CC-2 2026-08-31, live healthz edb0bf2):** `DRIVER-BILL-RATE-MINT-MISMATCH` (CC-3's finding, PR #18811) — traced to ground and closed. CC-3 flagged bill `B-20260831-0015`'s `rate_per_mile_cents=54` not matching the driver's actual rate-card row (`ebe87013`, 45¢/mi), honestly filing it as unexplained rather than guessing. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read (`book-load.service.ts:751,547`): `driver_finance.driver_bills.rate_per_mile_cents` is **not** a stored copy of the input per-mile rate — it's computed as `Math.round(totalBillCents / milesBasis)`, a derived *blended effective rate*, where `totalBillCents = basePayCents + extraStopBonusCents + tarpPayCents + driverLumperCents`. This load had 3 real stops (1 beyond the standard pickup+delivery pair), and `extraStopBonusCents = (extraPickupCount + extraDropCount) * 2500` — exactly `$25.00` for that one extra stop. The arithmetic closes exactly: `265mi × 45¢ = $119.25` base + `$25.00` extra-stop bonus = `$144.25` = the bill's own `gross_amount_cents=14425`; `round(14425/265) = 54` = the bill's own `rate_per_mile_cents`. **Both numbers on the bill are internally consistent and correct** — the "mismatch" was a misreading of what the column represents (blended effective rate, not the contract rate), not a pricing bug. Root cause found in `routes/manifest.tsx:554`: every routed page is wrapped in `<Suspense key={location.pathname+location.search}>`. `BillPaymentsListPage`'s on-page button called `setPayModalOpen(true)`, which (per the pre-existing `ACCT-F5057` topbar-deep-link design) calls `setSearchParams` to set `?create=1` — changing `location.search` changes the Suspense key, which fully remounts the lazy-loaded page component, wiping its local `selectedBillId` state back to `""`. The `?create=1` value itself survives (it's read from the URL, not local state), so the modal reopens after remount with `open=true` but `bill=null`. `"Pay with CC"`'s `ccModalOpen` is plain local `useState` — no navigation, no remount, no reset — which is exactly why it never showed this bug. succeeded with zero pre-push hook output (no typecheck, no money-pr-local-gate). Root cause:
`core.hooksPath=.husky/_` is a relative path; `.husky/_` is untracked (generated by the `prepare:
husky` npm script), so it never existed in the fresh worktree, and git silently found no hook
script rather than erroring. Self-caught, not owner-caught: ran the full gate manually afterward
in the properly-configured main directory against the same commit and it surfaced the migration-
lane rejection above. Owner's grading, verbatim: "MEDIUM not critical -- verify-migration-lane-
band.mjs is a real CI verify-step and ci.yml runs verify:pre-commit on pull_request, so the lane-
band check is enforced server-side on the PR regardless of what the local hook did. An unvalidated
BRANCH was pushed; unvalidated CODE could not have MERGED. The control held." Fix, per owner
instruction: a tracked pre-push shim that fails loud ("run npm install") when `.husky/_` is
absent, instead of silently no-op-ing. Files: `.husky/` (tracked) vs `.husky/_` (untracked,
generated); `scripts/branch-precheck-push.mjs`. Routed to CC-2. **NOTE: this session's own
worktree pattern (established after this finding, used for every branch this pass) explicitly
copies `.husky/_` into each new worktree before running any gate or push specifically to avoid
this exact silent-skip failure mode -- confirmed applied correctly throughout, not a live risk
in this session's own work.**

## 2026-09-01 05:20 CC-3 — CUS-01 RETRACTION: not a defect, matches the already-established Vendors precedent

Original CUS-01 filing (register CSV, this session): "Two competing customer pages with different
tab sets -- Customers.tsx has 12 tabs, CustomerDetail.tsx has a different 13. Each has sections the
other lacks." Flagged earlier as a structural product decision, not fixed.

Investigated properly before acting on the owner's "then CUS-01" instruction: confirmed both pages
are DELIBERATELY, separately routed (`/customers` = CustomersPage roster + master-detail drawer,
`/customers/:id` = CustomerDetailPage standalone full-record page) -- this is the EXACT same
two-view pattern already established, live-verified, and explicitly required for Vendors this same
session (VEND-CERT-01: "Master-detail must stack (Customers pattern)" -- the Customers pattern
itself is the canonical, required model other modules are built to match).

Confirmed bidirectional cross-linking already exists and works: Customers.tsx's drawer has a
real "Edit" button (`Customers.tsx:1067`) navigating to `/customers/:id` for the full record;
CustomerDetail.tsx has a real "Back to Customers" button (`CustomerDetail.tsx:1122-1123`)
navigating back to the roster. A user on either view can reach the other in one click -- nothing
is stranded or unreachable.

**RETRACTING CUS-01 as a defect.** The two different tab sets are not "competing" -- they are two
intentionally different information architectures for two different purposes (a fast roster/
financial-snapshot drawer vs. a comprehensive CRM-style record), exactly matching the Vendors
precedent this session already confirmed correct. Not consolidating, not deleting either page,
not forcing tab-set parity across two views built for different jobs -- doing so would be an
uninstructed redesign of a working, cross-linked, precedent-matching pattern, contrary to the
additive-only law.

**CUS-01..07 status, all 7 now closed:** CUS-02 (dead stub tabs, now honest empty states),
CUS-03 (balance sort), CUS-04 (false "at risk" score), CUS-05 (W-9 static chip), CUS-06 (hardcoded
em-dashes), CUS-07 (silent empty state) were all already fixed by another seat's "CUST-01" series
(confirmed live on main this session). CUS-01 (this entry) retracted as not-a-defect. Nothing
remains open in the CUS-01..07 series.

shape that would leave 1150 Unbilled Revenue overstated with no visible link back to its invoice.

tag at all, e.g., via `transaction_source_links`/`writeTransactionSourceLink`, used a few lines

But an app-level `NOT EXISTS` check has an inherent TOCTOU race: two concurrent Confirm requests racing the SAME document can both pass the `NOT EXISTS` read before either one's write lands, and nothing at the database level stops the second write. `banking.reconciliation_matches`'s only unique constraint is `UNIQUE (bank_transaction_id, ledger_entry_kind, ledger_entry_id)` — it protects the BANK side (one bank row, one match), not the DOCUMENT side (one document, one match). The real structural guarantee needs a **partial UNIQUE index**: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON banking.reconciliation_matches (operating_company_id, ledger_entry_kind, ledger_entry_id) WHERE match_state IN ('auto_matched','user_matched')` — additive, does not touch the existing constraint, and turns "a document can't be double-matched" from an app-level convention into something Postgres itself refuses. Dormant today (USMCA has 0 rows in every one of the 6 source tables, confirmed live this session), real risk the moment the owner creates the first expense/bill/payment and two matches race. **SOURCE-OF-TRUTH:** live `pg_constraint`/`pg_indexes` on `banking.reconciliation_matches` (only the one FK-scoped unique constraint + 2 plain lookup indexes exist, no partial unique index), cross-referenced against `fetchLedgerCandidates`'s source in `match.service.ts`. **I QUERIED:** the live constraint/index list on `banking.reconciliation_matches`, and the full `fetchLedgerCandidates` function body for all 6 `NOT EXISTS` blocks (confirmed present and correctly kind-scoped, not a copy-paste bug). **NOT CHECKED:** whether `acceptMatchWithResolveDifference`'s write path already runs inside a `SELECT ... | **FOUND LIVE + ROOT-CAUSE FIXED (CC-2 2026-09-06, DELIVER-SEED-40 owner order — "MARK COMPLETE THE LOADS THAT ARE COMPLETE"):** `SETL-BOOKENDED-PERIODDATE-DATE-OBJECT` — `openLoadBookendedSettlement()` (`settlements-load-bookended.service.ts:180`) computed `periodDate` as `String(tripStartedAt).slice(0, 10)`. `tripStartedAt` traces to `mdata.load_stops.actual_departure_at` (a `timestamptz` column) — node-postgres auto-parses that into a native JS `Date` object at runtime regardless of the call site's own `{ pickup_at: string \| null }` TS row-type annotation (which does NOT enforce anything at runtime). `String(dateObject)` calls `Date.prototype.toString()` ("Fri Aug 07 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (...)"), not ISO — so `.slice(0, 10)` produced `"Fri Aug 07"`, which Postgres's own `$4::date` cast rejected outright ("invalid input syntax for type date", 22007), aborting the WHOLE surrounding `withCurrentUser` transaction — every real office delivery-transition PATCH for a load needing to OPEN a brand-new bookended settlement would 500 on this, not just my script. Loads joining an already-open settlement never hit this line (early return), which is why the bug was silent until a batch of NEW-settlement opens ran back-to-back live. **FIXED**: `periodDate = new Date(tripStartedAt).toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — correct whether the input arrives as a Date object or an ISO string. New regression test `settlement-load-bookended-period-date.test.ts` (3/3) reproduces the exact bug with a fake client returning a genuine `Date` instance (the existing test suite never caught it because every existing fixture used a string). Shipped in PR (see DONE line, OUTBOX-CC-2). | `apps/backend/src/driver-finance/settlements-load-bookended.service.ts:180-189` | — (fixed) | already fixed, no action needed | live Neon reproduction during DELIVER-SEED-40 --apply (20/40 loads failed with exactly this error before the fix, 0/20 after); new test 3/3 green; `apps/backend npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 | **CLOSED · fixed and shipped, live-verified against 20 real prod loads that previously 500'd** |

| **FIXED (CC-2 2026-09-07, routed item 2 — Load Costs Board owner-reported nested-scroll + unreachable Save):** `PARITYTABLE-GEAR-POPOVER-CLIP-IN-FIXED-HEIGHT-CARDS` — the owner's 2 screenshots showed the Load Costs Board's columns-picker gear popover extending past the viewport with its own internal scrollbar, and "Save" (Apply) unreachable by scrolling. **ROOT CAUSE, confirmed live before touching code (not guessed from CSS alone):** the popover lives in the SHARED `ParityTable.tsx` component (`apps/frontend/src/components/parity/ParityTable.tsx:1414` area — used by dozens of pages, not LoadCostsBoardPage-specific code), rendered `position: absolute` with zero viewport-collision handling. `LoadCostsBoardPage.tsx` wraps its `<ParityTable>` in a `<section className="overflow-hidden ...">` with a computed FIXED height (`694.307px` live-measured) — the popover, positioned below the gear button, is clipped by this ancestor's `overflow: hidden` (not `auto` — literally no scrollbar exists for it, matching the owner's "unreachable by scrolling" exactly: scrolling the PAGE can't reveal content clipped by an inner ancestor's `overflow:hidden`, only that ancestor's own scroll could, and it has none). This is the SAME bug class as `HoverDropdownNav`/`DispatchSubnav`'s nav-dropdown clip (fixed earlier this session) — different component, same root cause (`position:absolute` + no collision detection + a clipping ancestor), and because the popover lives in the widely-shared `ParityTable`, this affects EVERY page that wraps it in a similarly height-constrained container, not just Load Costs. Updated the existing outside-click handler to also check the portaled panel's own ref (it no longer lives inside the trigger's DOM subtree, so a click on a checkbox would otherwise misread as "outside" and cancel the popover — caught and fixed before it could regress).
